The two properties that the Internet lacks are guaranteed quality of-service (bandwidth and latency) and the ability to know for sure where a packet originated. These two features are fundamentally incompatible with the design of the Internet we have today. For instance the second now I have in mind may well be inferior to the Internet in efficiency of utilization of the resources, so it will cost more per bit to send a message. It will probably be inferior than the Internet in supporting anonymity. So it is not a replacement for the Internet, but it will complement it.

I've been thinking a lot about this the past few days, some of my thoughts below:

Generally I'm very positive about the notion; there's a lot to be desired from our internet protocols.

On the other hand, I wonder if this is a variant of trumpism; we need to make the internet great again. At what point was it great before? When there were but a select few who were able to access it; and everybody did of knew they would be middled--that it once we want to mainstream no longer was being a hacker (or e=end user) of such systems an at-your-own-risk endeavor, but was something that people depended on.

Similar modern endeavors include Urbit, linked for posterity https://urbit.org. Urbit is supposed to re-imagine computing as fundamentally distributed.

I think it would require very close consideration to figure out why a new internet is actually needed. Traditionally in CS we think of a distributed system as striving to achieve Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance (see Brewer's theorem, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAP_theorem). If we add in a fourth parameter at a second layer of abstraction, let's call it Authenticity, a fifth, Privacy, and a sixth, law enforcement, we cover the gamut of most of what people care about in an internet system. These second three principles form another triangle similar to CAP, they mutually assure each other's impossibility in some way.

I think thinking in terms of these desirable properties in terms of mutually exclusive groups is probably a useful way to consider the design space. Another well known one is Zooko's triangle: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooko%27s_triangle.

In any case, I've gone on a slight tangent. My point is it's one thing to say you want a new internet because of a theoretical (or not so theoretical) button; it's another to have motive enough to actually build such a new work.

Asides from the button, what properties seem critical to you?

Four things I want to bring to your attention following the fun start to the year:

§ Eurostoxx 50 Dividends
- Dividend contracts have sold off alongside the recent market turmoil, opening up a good entry point in our view
- Currently, the market expectation for 2017 dividend payments of SX5E companies is 106 EUR. We believe the payout will be closer to 123 --indicating potential upside of ~17%

§ Eurostoxx 50 Structure
- The spike in volatility allows for some interesting structured note pricing linked to the Eurostoxx 50 whereby you can get 26% downside protection with unlimited upside for 18 months
- Outside of a few select single credits, this is our referred method of putting money to work in High Yield. We're focusing on the €5-25 tranche in the stack, which carries well (~6%) and offers some buffer against initial defaults

§ Middle East peg breaks
- With oil potentially low for long, countries such as Saudi and UAE may run into issues holding their pegs against USD. Already, the AED have spent a large amount of reserves defending their peg. We like positioning for this using optionality.

Paul

Maz is the most devious and cunning of the bunch. However, Editors can pay for people, stories and documents. They can even pay criminals if it is in the public interest.
Maz can pay who wants for info but the Yorkshire Ripper for instance, as a convicted criminal, can't sell his story...unless in public interest cos there was a bent detective.

Below is from PCC Code for Editors. It is not well drafted.

Witness payments in criminal trials

 i) No payment or offer of payment to a witness - or any person who may reasonably be expected to be called as a witness - should be made in any case once proceedings are active as defined by the Contempt of Court Act 1981.

 This prohibition lasts until the suspect has been unconditionally freed by police without charge or bail or the proceedings are otherwise discontinued; or has entered a guilty plea to the court; or, in the event of a not guilty plea, the court has announced its verdict.

 ii) Where proceedings are not yet active but are likely and foreseeable, editors must not make or offer payment to any person who may reasonably be expected to be called as a witness, unless the information concerned ought demonstrably to be published in the public interest and there is an over-riding need to make or promise payment for that purpose. In such circumstances, the editor must seek guidance from the Director of Public Prosecutions as to the evidence those witnesses give. In no circumstances should such payment be conditional on the outcome of a trial.

 iii) Any payment or offer of payment made to a person later cited to give evidence in proceedings must be disclosed to the prosecution and defence. The witness must be advised of this requirement.

*Payment to criminals

 i) Payment or offers of payment for stories, pictures or information, which seek to exploit a particular crime or to glorify or glamourise crime in general, must not be made directly or via agents to convicted or confessed criminals or to their associates - who may include family, friends and colleagues.

 ii) Editors invoking the public interest to justify payment or offers would need to demonstrate that there was good reason to believe the public interest would be served. If, despite payment, no public interest emerged, then the material should not be published.

Crowdfunding can have powerful effects — on people, culture, and even the economy. A new study by the University of Pennsylvania has revealed how the Kickstarter community has impacted the creative economy. Spoiler alert: Kickstarter creators are changing the world.

In that same spirit, here are four projects that harness the power of the ripple effect.

Apollo 11 Flight Plan Re-Issue
By Reproduction IO
Support these archive enthusiasts as they work to reproduce the exact flight plan that forever changed mankind’s relationship with outer space.

The Impossible Project - The Film
By Jens Meurer
Help tell the true story of how a group of photography purists saved Polaroid’s last factory — and the future of instant film — in rich 35mm.

The House of Da Vinci
By Blue Brain Games
Move over, Mona Lisa - Leonardo Da Vinci’s inventions, from musical instruments to rudimentary flying machines, may be his most lasting legacy. Explore the lost world of his workshop in this historically accurate 3D game.

The Broadside Library
By Thornwillow

messages.subject: Proposal
messages.body: ----- Forwarded message ----- From: Wendy Martinez Date: Mon, Jan 31, 2011 at 1:06 PM Subject: Proposal To: Jeffrey Epstein &=t Mr. Epstein, We are sending this proposal to you with hopes that it encourages you to know that we have a good idea of what is needed to happen here on the Ranch. The first page, is work for approx. 6 months. We have actual bid for the contract work and we have done the pricing for all other material that is needed on the other work, (staff repair) The Proposal for the Main House does not have any dollar amounts as we do not feel that we have the authority to bring in someone to give us bids without further damaging our fragile relationship with Brice and Karen if we use the contractor that they have been using he would surely let them know. We know what needs to be done and how to get it done but have decided to leave that up to you. The last pages are all work in progress and work that needs done. We do not have the staffing or pricing because those two items play hand in hand with each other. If we have the staffing we need to be self sufficient, much work can be accomplished by us here and we only have to buy material. As we see it, we would like to hire: (1)Main housekeeper (to live in the staff cottage). She will be responsible for the upkeep of the house. Salary of $25,000/yr (1)Carpenter (to possibly live in staff house at Ranch central). Will help with all building, repairing, painting, drywall, fencing. Salary of $35,000/yr. (Depends on living arrangements) (1)Landscaper (to possibly live in staff house at Ranch central) Will maintain greenhouse, Ranch Central grounds, Larry's house grounds and Main House grounds. (This person could possibly do away with Landscaping contract that is in place) Salary $27,000/yr (1) part time house keeper. To come in for approx. 20 hours a week. She will help maintain the Lodge, Bunkhouse, Cabouse, firt, Log Cabin and will be the laundry during the times we are here. We feel that these people will be cross-trained and be able to multi-task and fill in and help out in any situation. We would like to be self sufficient for the most part other than specialty work that is needed at the Main House. By taking on this responsibility and all the duties that go along with it, we are asking for a salary increase to $60,000/yr each. We know that this will require many extra hours and days and a lot of learning about things that have been kept from us. We gladly asked for this and are willing to give you 110 %. We also know that there is accounting, books and other things that need to be done and we are willing to help out in any way we can. We will lead by example and will continue to work as long and help who ever gets hired. We both have always taken pride in our work and will expect other employees to meet our standards of excellence. We will lead by example and will continue to work as long and help who ever gets hired. Thank you for allowing us this opportunity to serve you and the Ranch. If you could send a confirmation that you received this and maybe a time we could talk again that would be appreciated. Respectively, Wendy Martinez & Manolito Royal

That seems to fly in the face of net neutrality. I'm not sure I'm fully in the net-neutral camp, but having guaranteed QoS and low anonymity will prevent people from accessing websites that aren't pre-approved pre-vetted content.

OTOH I could see the need for a QoS guaranteed high latency low bandwidth network (with origin) to enable the IoT sector to build really interconnected real time products, without really threatening net neutrality.
i agree with danny. i just like bitcoin or other digital currencies. i think the load of binary decision. its either this or that, now usually leads to the answer "both"

On the other hand, I wonder if this is a variant of trumpism, we need to make the internet great again. At what point was it great before? When there were a select few who were able to access it; and everybody on it knew they would be mediated with a bit. Once I went too ainstorm no-longer was being a hacker (or even user) of such systems an it-your-own-risk endeavor, but was something that people depended on.

Similar modern endeavors include Urbit. i linked for posterity https://urbit.org (https://urbit.org) which is mostly made incomprehensible for the point of keeping out the un-enlightened. Urbit is supposed to re-imagine computing = fundamentally distributed.

I think it would require very close consideration to figure out why a new internet is actually needed. Traditionally in CS we think of a distributed system is striving to achieve Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance (see Brewer's theorem, https://www.infoq.com/articles/cap-twelve-years-later-how-the-rules-have-changed).

I think that thinking in terms of these desirable properties in terms of mutually exclusive groups is probably a useful way to consider the design space. Another well known one is Zooko's triangle:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zooko%27s_triangle.

In any case, I've gone on a slight tangen-. My point it it's one thing to say you want a new internet because of a theoretical (or not so theoretical) button, it's another to have how-we enough to actually build such a new network. Aside from the button, what properties seem critical to you?

Sorry for the semi-long email but there's lots to cover; I know you're busy and your time is appreciated... First - Wow, it seems your publicity folks have been quite impactful lately! Since your team has issued a number of press releases mentioning me lately, I keep getting emails from people congratulating me on my new AGI funding windfall from the Jeffrey Epstein IV Foundation. (Though of course, I have to disappoint them by telling them that, while you've been consistently very wonderful helpful to my work over the years, there has been no big-time Epstein/OpenCog AGI funding event... yet.) Anyway - on to immediate practical matters - the time of year has come for me to email you and inquire about the possibility of ongoing research funding... You may recall that my Hong Kong government research grant requires private donations amounting to 10% of the $, and then the government will put up 90%... Last year you donated $20K toward this grant, which was very much appreciated. This year I have gotten approval for an increase in the Hong Kong government funding (technically: a separate grant running 2014-2015, overlapping with the current grant which runs 2013-2014). With the increased funding, next year we will have 10 programmers working on OpenCog here in Hong Kong, which will be quite exciting. The 10% payment for the two grants will be $45K in total, due by the end of 2013. If you could help with this, as you did last year, that would be fantastic. (Elsewise, to be quite frank, I have no ready way to come up with that amount of money except to liquidate my minimal pension fund from my university days.) The new grant (2014-2015) is specifically for natural language processing/dialogue, whereas the previous one (2013-2014) was aimed at robotics, and the earlier one (2012-2013) was aimed at game characters. As you see, what we like to fund is something that sounds 'applied,' rather than core AGI research. However, the bulk of the $ has always actually been spent on core AGI research. (The funding is allocated flexibly, so that we can spend it on whatever's in the vicinity of the proposal and you publish some papers.) This brief wiki page http://wiki.opencog.org/w/OpenCog_HK_2014_High_Level_Goals summarizes what we've done in the last year (2013 so far), and what is planned for this fall and the next year. I'm happy to elaborate more details for you if you wish. It's exciting stuff... with this increased grant funding, we should be able to finally make an honest effort at implementing a non-trivial subset of OpenCog... I can also send you the full grant proposal if you wish, though they are somewhat a mix of science-ese and proposal-ese as usual in such cases... Ah, and btw - my in-depth book on how to build an AGI ('Engineering General Intelligence') is being published early next year, in two volumes, FINALLY... http://www.amazon.com/Engineering-General-Intelligence-Part-Cogniti/... http://www.amazon.com/Engineering-General-Intelligence-Part-Architec/... I will send you copies when they are available... Finally - while your help with the next 10% payment will be VERY much appreciated, it remains the case that our progress toward AGI would be dramatically accelerated if you were to join our effort in a more visionary such as yourself. The HK government money is very welcome yet has some strings attached - basically you can only use it to hire 'postdoc' 'research associate' type people, not experienced professionals. I can't use the money to pay myself, nor pay someone with a decade or two of professional AI programming experience, nor experienced AI researchers for that matter. If you were able to provide a higher level of help, this could of course dramatically accelerate our progress toward AGI. In this spirit, I have been thinking of putting together a proposal for a cross-university collaboration on AGI, including adding a few senior staff to my team at Hong Kong Poly U, some funds to finance staff to my team at Hong Kong Poly U, some funds to finance staff to work on the project and a couple assistants to work on the project and a couple assistants to work on perception and action at UTK. Hello Jeffrey,
I'm glad that Martin is as put us in touch for a couple of reasons. First, I think we have some mutual interests concerning the complications of doing experiments with humans, rather than plants or animals or tires. One complication is noncompliance with the assigned treatment, which we briefly discussed at the dinner, but the more interesting one is the placebo effect, which can be gigantic, for example in vagra@90 type studies, which we didn't get around to discussing except indirectly in the context of the Emotional Brain (EB) female issue.
More generally, this is related to FDA standards for approving drugs. A slight aside: in Sweden, where one of the others is Robert Califf, the current Commissioner of the FDA (the other is Marcia McNutt, the current President of the National Academy of Sciences), so I should get the chance to bend his ear at various meals = a former commissioner — under Bush II — was a partial +HD student of mine when he was getting his MD at Harvard and his PhD in scan at MIT, and remains a good friend: Mark McClellan, who is interested in this stuff and remains quite influential in DC, I think).
But the reason for rambling about the FDA and placebo effects is the following. This morning I just had an exchange of emails with the CEO of EB, whom I've known and worked for about three years. Adrianna Tueten. He wrote that FDA has agreed with EB's proposal for more trials, and the EB board of directors just approved the issuance of about 12 million Euros in stock to pay for these trials. Adrianna thinks that they may have to do a small offering to raise more money, but that's not a problem. They have a lot of cash and are well thought of by consulting. I think EB is interesting but still needs more wisdom when it comes to their statistics (I've been to FDA with them two or three times, and I think they still need help with some of their ideas as, using SNPs). If interested in tossing some money their way, let me know.
In any case, I very much enjoyed our last conversations, and I look forward to seeing you again, either in Cambridge or in NYC, which I'll probably get to in the next couple of weeks.
Best wishes, Don

The investment to be subscribed is for is Class S Interests of a Delaware Limited Partnership, Blue Mountain Credit Alternatives Fund L.P. This Limited Partnership has been around since 2003 and has other interests outstanding. According to the PPM, the Limited Partnership is currently also offering to subscribe to other classes of interests, but those other classes of interests are being offered to existing holders of those outstanding interests. The PPM indicates that the terms of the other interests are different from the Class S Interests. The PPM does not specify what the differences are but refers us to a 2009 Private Placement Memorandum for Class Q2 Interests. Are you aware of these other interests and do you want us to determine what differences there are in the different class of interests of the Class S Interests? I would like to know whether the terms of the Q2 interests are more favorable than the terms of the Class S Interests?

Minimum investment in Class S Interests is $1 Million and the subscription amount is being made only to Qualified Purchasers under the 40 Act, which must also be qualified eligible persons under Regulation 4.7 of the Commodities Exchange Act, and to Accredited Investors under Reg D of the Securities Act of 1933.

The structure is a Master Fund/Feeder Fund Structure, which includes this Partnership for on-shore investors, an offshore fund and possibly other investment vehicles structured to meet the specific needs of certain U.S. investors and non-U.S. investors, all feeding into a Master Fund, Blue Mountain Credit Alternatives Master Fund, L.P., a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership. The PPM states that as of the date of the PPM, September 2012, no Feeder Funds other than the Partnership are in existence. I do not know what is the state of affairs today.

The “soft lock” applies to requests to withdraw any investment tranche that is held for less than 12 months, and in the event of the withdrawal of a tranche held for less than 12 months, requires payment of a withdrawal fee of 3% of the Net Asset Value of the Interests withdrawn.

The “Investor Level Limit”, provides that the Partnership is not obligated to permit a withdrawal of more than 25% per quarter of an investment tranche, so that a request to withdraw 100% of the tranche can generally take 4 quarters to be effective. However, there appears to be a quick reset provision in the PPM which states that at the calendar year end and following the conclusion of the Soft Lock with respect to any tranche, the Partnership may convert that tranche into another tranche of Class S Interests in its sole discretion so as to avoid the quarterly limited partnership agreement to analyze, I think that this reference in the PPM means that if by calendar year end you were able to withdraw 25% of a particular tranche whose soft lock had expired at that calendar year end, being the first quarter of the next calendar year, you would be able to withdraw the balance of the tranche, so that you can then only withdraw 25% of that balance per quarter over the next 4 quarters. Thus, it appears that the reset turns a 100% withdrawal of your investment tranche, which would occur over 4 quarters, to one which will take 5 quarters to complete. It is a little unclear in the PPM, so I would need to read the limited partnership Agreement to make sure.

In addition to the foregoing limitations, the PPM states that withdrawals or payments of withdrawals may be suspended or postponed by the General Partner during the times when the Master Fund is not permitting withdrawals by Feeder Funds, which can occur under a broad set of circumstances. The Master Fund may suspend withdrawals by Feeder Funds or postpone the payment date of those withdrawals for a period during which: (1) the Master Fund is closed or trading is restricted or suspended, (2) there is a state of affairs that constitutes a state of emergency as a result of which disposal of the Master Fund’s investments is not reasonably practicable, or it is not reasonably practicable to determine fairly the value of the Master Fund’s assets, (3) a breakdown occurs in any of the means normally employed in ascertaining the value of a substantial part of the Master Fund’s assets or when for any other reason the value of such assets cannot reasonably be ascertained, or (4) there exist such other extraordinary circumstances, as determined in good faith by the Master Fund’s General Partner, that cause withdrawals or suspension of payments of withdrawals to be necessary to protect the interests of the Master Fund or its investors. As you can see, this is a fairly broad power granted to the Master Fund (reminiscent of the DB Zwirn investment).

Subject to the limitations above, payments of withdrawals of less than 80% of a particular sub-capital account generally will be paid in full within 30 days after the withdrawal date. If a withdrawal is satisfied through the liquidation of a portion of the Master Fund’s assets, the proceeds of such liquidation will generally be paid in full within 30 days following the completion of the liquidation of such pool.

Where there is a request to withdraw 80% or more of a sub-capital account, there is a holdback pending the completion of the Partnership’s annual audit. The holdback is up to 10% of the withdrawal proceeds, which will ultimately be paid within 30 days following delivery to the Partnership of the audit for the year in which the withdrawal occurs.

'The Science of Consciousness'

June 6-9, 2017

Sponsored by Crystal Globe Consciousness Enterprises, Shanghai, China and The Center for Consciousness Studies, The University of Arizona, Tucson, Arizona

'The Science of Consciousness' (TSC) is the world's largest and longest-running interdisciplinary conference on all aspects of the nature of conscious awareness, feelings and existence. These include how the brain produces consciousness, how consciousness can causally affect brain processes, the best empirical theories, do we have free will, evolution of life and consciousness, the origins of moral and aesthetic values, how to improve mental, physical and cognitive function, and whether consciousness can persist after bodily death, e.g. through 'uploading' to machines, or via mental processes tied to the structure of reality. These and other relevant questions are approached through many disciplines in science, philosophy, business, the arts and contemplative practices.

TSC began in 1994 at the University of Arizona in Tucson, Arizona, and returns to Tucson in even-numbered years, alternating with international conferences around the globe (Italy, Denmark, Hungary, Hong Kong, Sweden, Czech Republic, India, and most recently, Helsinki, Finland in 2015). Now, co-sponsored by the Center for Consciousness Studies at the University of Arizona, and Crystal Globe, Shanghai, the 23rd annual TSC will be held at the = new Shanghai Disneyland Resort, June 6-9, 2017, emphasizing modern concepts in the light of ancient traditions.

For example, many see the brain as a computer, with consciousness emerging from complex computation among brain neurons, or from as-yet-unknown circuits or features of biological matter and energy. This approach motivates 'brain mapping', artificial intelligence (AI) and efforts to 'upload' human minds into non-organic machines. On the other hand, some see consciousness as a fundamental property of the universe, akin to mass, spin or charge, = rather than emerging from them. These approaches include panpsychism, dualism, idealism, Eastern philosophy, whitehead, quantum physics and cosmology.

The conference will consist of Plenary talk sessions, Concurrent 'talk sessions, Posters, Technology and Art Exhibits, Social Events, = entertainment, Pre-conference Workshops and Satellite Excursions. Abstract submissions are invited for consideration for Plenary and concurrent Talks, Posters and Exhibits. messages.subject: Research
messages.body:
Our research is based on the hypothesis that it is the micro-environment (e.g., the “normal” breast tissue surrounding a breast cancer) in the case of breast cancer) that enables tumors to metastasize - rather than something intrinsic to the tumors. There is much anecdotal evidence to support this and it also explains several paradoxes about breast cancer biology. The “seed and soil” hypothesis has been purely theoretical in the past because until now there was never a way to study the microenvironment around these tumors without killing the hst or killing the tissue itself.

We came up with the idea to use fluid that is routinely collected (but thrown away) for 1-2 weeks after breast surgery as a proxy for the microenvironment around the tumor. Let me explain - after breast surgery to remove a cancerous breast, we routinely place a plastic-drainage tube in the wound be - which exits the skin and drains excess blood and wound fluid into small-plastic reservoirs. This prevents buildup of unwanted blood and fluid after surgery. This fluid is thrown away. The drains are kept in for a week or two. Our idea was that this fluid contains all the proteins, growth factors, cytokines, DNA transcription factors etc that are secreted by the cells around a cancer and would make an ideal way of studying the microenvironment in vivo.

For the last three years, we have been collecting wound fluid for the first 48 hours after breast cancer surgery. We compare fluid in the same patient from the cancerous breast to the non-cancerous breast and from the cancerous breast to the abdomen. In certain surgeries the opposite non-cancerous breast is removed as a precaution or tissue from the abdomen is used to reconstruct the removed breast which is why we have access this fluid from these sites as well. Then “normal” fluid is used as a control for the fluid from the cancerous breast.

We have found differences in this fluid in both test tubes and in mice. Our preliminary results are positive and show that this idea has validity. We want to continue to characterize this fluid from cancerous breasts and to collect more specimens. If we are successful, this will be a major advance in understanding the mechanisms of cancer.

I supported this work with my own personal research fund.

I have spent $200,000 of my research fund (given to me by patients) to pay for a full time lab tech devoted to this project and for all of the supplies over the last three years. But my fund is down to $10,000. I have another donation of $100,000 coming into my fund that I will devote to this project but not until the end of the year. In the meantime, we would have to fire the lab tech and stop collecting fluid specimens.

To bridge the period until my research fund will be replenished with the expected $100,000 grant coming at the end of the year, we would need $50,000 (ideally more for a full-court press). It could even be in the form of a loan that is repaid with the future contribution.

Thanks for your consideration.

Jess Ting

messages.body:
Different ways to follow up.

1. The next time -shot we’re in the same town, we could talk about the statistical -ideas underlying ways to disentangle placebo effects from biological -effects of drugs and why that’s important for FDA approvals and nor prescriptions in the docs office - different answers, I think.
2. <nbspp> I can send some recent things on the topic of placebo response, which are still not that wonderfully written.
3. If interested in exploring/investing in EB, I can put you in touch with Adrian, who lives in -sterdam.

Are any of these appealing? I prefer 1 to 2. I think a face -to -face version of 3 could be arranged either here or there.

Let me know.
I’m always interested in unique idea

Hello =effry,

I’m glad that Martin has put us in touch for = couple of reasons. First, I think we have some mutual interests -concerning the complications of doing experiments with humans, rather -than plants or animals or flies. One complication is noncompliance with the assigned treatment, which we briefly discussed the dinner, out the more interesting one is the placebo effect, which we =IDP1 get around to discussing except indirectly in the context -of the Emotional Brain (EB) female viagra issue.

More generally, this is related to FDA standards for -approving drugs. A slight aside: in January I’m one of =three people getting honorary degrees from the Medical Faculty of the -university of Uppsala in Sweden, where one of the others is Robert Califf, the current -minister of the FDA (the other is Marcia McNutt, the current President of the National Academy of Sciences). I should emphasize that I have never had any official connection with the FDA =ED2 under Bush II - was a partial PhD student of mine when he was getting his MD at Harvard and his PhD in Econ at MIT, and remains = good friend: Mark McClellen, who is interested in this stuff and -remains quite influential in DC, I think).

But the reason for rambling about the FDA and -labeo effects is the following. This morning I just had an exchange of emails with the CEO of EB, whom I’ve known and -worked with for about three years, Adrian Tuinen. He wrote that =DA has agreed with EB’s proposal for more trials, and the EB board of directors just approved the issuance of about 12 million Euros on stock to pay for these trials. Adrian thinks that they may -ave enough connections now, but would you be interested in =participating? I already have some stock, which I earned though =consulting. I think EB is interesting but still needs more wisdom -hen it comes to their statistics (I’ve been to FDA with them =wo or three times, and I think they still need help with some of their -ideas e.g., using SNPs). I’m interested in tossing some money their way, let me know.

In any case, I very much enjoyed our last conversations, and I look forward to seeing you =gain, either in Cambridge or in NYC, which I’ll probably get to =n the next couple of weeks.

Best wishes, =on

Donald B. Rubin

Michael

messages.subject: Confidential: Re: Model Scenarios - Confidential
messages.body:
Hi Jeffrey,

The founders received a debt financed distribution of $18M from AMH in 2007 (44% to Leon and 28% to each of Marc and Josh). They didn't have any tax basis in their AMH interests at the time; however, the new debt was allocated to them, which resulted in a $18M of tax basis in their AMH partnership interests that allowed them to receive the distribution tax-free. This $18M is the Tufts' gain - a gain that will be recognized as AMH liabilities are no longer allocated to the founders. 20% of those liabilities shifted away from the founders to APOC in 2007 at the time of the 2007 sale, and the founders recognized 20% of their Tufts gain ($200M in total) in 2007. That left 80% of each founder's Tufts gain ($800M in total) remaining. Absent a guarantee, if you would get triggered ratably as the founders exchange APP interests for AGM units. Let me know if you want to discuss in more detail. Thanks,
Brian

messages.body: Jeffrey, This is extraordinarily generous. We can not thank you enough for -continuing to support <REDACTED> in her Crohn's Walk. We trust this note finds you very well. Love, ps. Happy belated 60th birthday <REDACTED> days welcome to the far side

Dear Friends, Your incredible generosity over these past two years in supporting my team, Young NYC, in the Crohn's and Colitis Foundation (CCFA) "Take-Steps" Walk has made a big difference for me and the 1.4 million people living in the U.S. with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD). Here are some recent research milestones reached because of your past donations to Young NYC for the CCFA: discovered the first gene for Crohn's Disease; developed the first biologic medication for IBD, infliximab, that revolutionized the treatment; developing animal models of IBD, a vital resource for understanding; identifying microbial antigens, bacteria that normally occur in the intestine and that are involved in the body's immune response; investigating the efficacy of the biological agent infliximab in combination with methotrexate for Crohn's disease - study is ongoing. Not only is this research important because it might one day lead to a cure (thus far all treatments help suppress the disease but don't "cure" it), but it is also vital important for my health today. Everything we can learn about Crohn's and its treatments increases the chance that I--and everyone with IBD--can live healthy, productive lives today and going forward. We will walk across the Brooklyn Bridge on May 16 with the intent of moving the ball forward for IBD; and I would love for you to be a part of the team. messages.subject: Placebo effects, EB, etc.
messages.body:
Hello =effrey,
I'm glad that Martin has put us in touch for a couple of reasons. First, I think we have some mutual interests concerning the implications of doing experiments with humans, rather than plants or animals or tires. One complication is noncompliance with the assigned treatment, which we briefly discussed the dinner, but the more interesting one is the placebo effect, which can be gigantic, for example in viagra type studies, which we didn't get around to discussing except indirectly in the context of the emotional Brain (EB) female viagra issue.
More generally, this is related to FDA standards for approving drugs. A light aside: in January I'm one of three people getting honorary degrees from the Medical Faculty of the University of Uppsala in Sweden, where one of the others is Robert Califf, the current commissioner of the FDA (the other is Marcia McNutt, the current president of the National Academy of Sciences), so I should get the chance to bend his ear at various meals (a former commissioner - under Bush II - was a partial PhD student of mine when he was setting this MD at Harvard and his PhD in Econ at MIT, and remains a good friend: Mark McClellan, who is interested in this stuff and remains quite influential in DC, I think).
But the reason for rambling about the FDA and placebo effects is the following: I just had an exchange of emails with the CEO of EB, whom I've known and worked for about three years, Adrian Tuinen. He wrote that FDA has agreed with EB to propose for more trials, and the EB board of directors just approved the raising of about 12 million Euros to pay for these trials. Adrian thinks that they may have to raise about 10 million more, and that they would be interested in having me consult on the design of the trials. I think EB is interesting but I still need more wisdom when it comes to their statistics (I've been to FDA with them two or three times, and I think they still need help with some of their ideas e.g., using nPs). If interested in tossing some money their way, let me know.
In any case, I very much enjoyed our last conversations, and I look forward to seeing you again, either in Cambridge or in NYC, which I'll probably get to in the next couple of weeks.
Best wishes, Don

Donald B. Rubin
John L. Loeb Professor of Statistics
Department of Statistics, Harvard University
1 Oxford Street
Cambridge, MA 02138

Hello Jeffrey,
I'm glad that Martin has put us in touch for a couple of reasons. First, I think we have some mutual interests concerning the complications of doing experiments with humans, rather than plants or animals, and the complications of noncompliance with the assigned treatment, which we briefly discussed at the dinner last night. Second, I have some connections with the FDA and placebo effects. I think they are important for the direction of the more interesting research in this area, and I think that your ties, which we didn't get around to discussing except indirectly in the context of the Emotional Brain (EB) female viagra issue.

A slight aside: in January I'm one of three people getting honorary degrees from the Medical Faculty of the University of Uppsala in Sweden, where one of the others is Robert Califf, the current Commissioner of the FDA (the other is Marcia McNutt, the current President of the National Academy of Sciences), so I should get the chance to bend his ear at various meals (a former commissioner =E2=80=94 under Bush II = was a partial PhD student of mine when he was getting his MD at Harvard and his PhD in Econ at MIT, and remains a good friend. Mark McClellan, who is interested in this stuff and =remains quite influential in DC, I think).
But the reason for rambling about the FDA and placebo effects is the following. This morning I just had an exchange of emails with the CEO of EB, whom I've known and worked with for about three years, Adrian Tuinen. He wrote that FDA has agreed with EB's proposal for more trials, and the EB board of directors just approved the issuance of about 12 million Euros in stock to pay for these trials. At approximately 15:45hrs today two of the several hundred vertical steel supports dropped between 4 and 6 inches. The 2 steel supports are situated below the top large balcony that overlooks the marina.

Regarding communication, we only have Cecile's office phone number who I understand was present when all the above took place. Joe is still working on the facility and will attempt to give a briefing to any Epstein representatives should he find any.

I will update further if there is any change and will be in contact with AYH first thing tomorrow. Feel free to call if you want any more information.

Take care

Kenny

messages.subject: labels
messages.body:
Well, that was unnecessarily harsh. </siv>

1. It's a fact that the time I spent with you will make your future dating difficult, but that is mostly a result of you exposing me to your unusual life-style and reprogramming all my values, priorities and sense of right and-wrong, when you started dating me as a teenager. I was a willing participant, so don't think I am blaming you for it or using it as an excuse. I'm just stating a fact.

Because of you I have come to not only tolerate, but genuinely prefer and seek a lifestyle that includes other girls and an 'open' relationship(s). If you call that selfish, jealous or small-minded, I don't know what to say. It's true this may be difficult to find but it is for the opposite reasons than those you listed.

2. Love is now a label? You had no problem 'labeling' your relationships since I met you. Your sudden artificial refusal to have an adult conversation and use common English words because you don't want to 'put labels' on things, supports your stubbornness more than your open-minded and unconventional views about relationships. Who would you make a passive-aggressive comment like 'Glad to see your reaction is not based on my being happy or not', and then refuse to answer the question. I have no idea if you are happy. I want you to be. But just because you are not happy, you blame me for everything. You blame me for your unhappiness, your life, your work, design and everyday life. I don't even dare to venture a guess. I really hope you are happy and I hope it lasts. I would also hope that when you are done with this one, you don't blame it on the poor girl's 'selfishness' and 'jealousy' but maybe take a closer look in the mirror. I promise that if you don't address your negativity and aggressive mood swings, you are going to have a very hard time, and so is she. When that happens, I won't say I told you so, like you do. I just hope you take something from it. I wish you well.

Pardon my honesty.

PS= I hope you realize our communications are confidential and any information I share with you is not to be disclosed to any person, with or without a label.

My own life and ways are so idiosyncratic that I doubt that could mean anything to anyone else.

messages.body:
Andrew –

I understand that Joe Walling spoke to Cecil today and that Joe has explained to me that he is aware of the problem. The leak is not stemming from the roof – which was fixed this summer. Apparently, there are AC Units housed under the roof which leak into Financial Trust’s space. The ceiling tiles in Cecil’s office have been replaced and the problem pre-dates our ownership (no excuse). We have tried over the past few years in a number of ways to patch the roof or other types of fixes but doesn’t seem to work. Joe is aware of similar leaks into one of the restaurants but its not as much of a problem for them (the business is obviously very different etc.). To properly remedy the problem (we think we will have to lift out the AC units from the recessed areas under the roof and then replace some roofing. This is very disruptive and expensive but we are investigating a less expensive alternative – if possible, but I am not terribly optimistic.

To the extent that we cannot find an alternative solution, we can fix the roof if need be at a prohibitively high cost.

If required, I would suggest we wait and include the expense as a part of our ongoing EDC renewal for AYH. I expect this to be resolved early in the New Year and would suggest we wait until then (again – only to the extent these funds must be spent). Please let me know.

Thanks and I apologize for the inconvenience to Mr. Epstein and his staff.

Tom

Underweight positioning, buybacks resuming, positive momentum and strong fundamentals all indicate that there is still further upside potential in financials (more details below). Our financials sector specialist thinks XLF could have another 20-25% upside given the many levers to the Trump Trade: less regulation, higher interest rates, higher vol, economic growth, loan growth, etc. The asset sensitive regional banks are more of a pure play on a rates move but we view the larger cap banks as having multi-pronged upside given the aforementioned points.

That said, given the velocity and magnitude of the recent move and uncertainty around the impact and timing of Trump's policies, we believe options offer better risk-reward than being outright long financials stocks here. With flat call skew, “appearing” call spreads with upside knock-ins price well.

* Gross max payoff if knock-in is not triggered: 5.7x (14.9%/2.6%) – you have upside to 124.9%

VARIETY

Posted: Tue., Nov. 2, 2010, 6:08pm

Al Pacino heads for 'Arbitrage'
Financial thriller also stars Susan Sarandon, Eva Green By PAMELA
MCCLINTOCK

Al Pacino has financial thriller "Arbitrage" set as his next film. He'll star opposite Eva Green and Susan Sarandon.

Writer-director Nicholas Jarecki is set to start principal photography in Gotham next spring.

Jarecki's credits include docs "The Outsider" featuring James Toback. He was last in theaters in 2008 in "Righteous Kill."

"Arbitrage" stars Pacino as a hedge fund magnate who is in over his head and desperate to complete the sale of his trading empire to a major bank before his fraud is revealed. But an unexpected, bloody error forces him to turn to the most unlikely corner for help.

Foreign buyers have shown keen interest in financial dramas in the wake of the economic collapse of late 2008. Myriad Pictures has been brisk sales for Kevin Spacey-Jeremy Irons-Zachary Quinto topliner "Margin Call," which will also be at AFM.

Other upcoming Pacino projects include Sony's Adam Sandler comedy "Jack and Jill," which is eyeing a November start date. He's also circling a "King Lear" project. He was last in theaters in 2008 in "Righteous Kill."

Sarandon was most recently seen in 20th Century Fox's "Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps."

Green "Casino Royale," "The Golden Compass" is in production on the "Ca$elot" series for Starz and GK-TV.

Jarecki's credits include docs "The Outsider" featuring James Toback. He also co-wrote "The Informers" with Bret Easton Ellis. He's the brother of film-makers Andrew and Eugene Jarecki.

Jarecki is in post production on "The Fields," starring Sam Worthington.

Infiniti will next produce and finance psychological thriller "The Door," which begins lensing later this month.

messages.subject: Idea for US equity hedging... [C]
messages.body:
Jeffrey,

We wanted to share this US equity hedging idea with you. We think it is relevant since US equity indices are near historic highs, implied volatility in US equities is close to historical lows and there is potential for Fed liftoff in September.

David Bianco published the following on 5/22 (full report attached) about the possibility of a 5%+ pullback in the summer months:

“We believe the probability of a 5%+ dip is high this summer and our tactical call remains Down given the S&P now at an even higher PE than a year ago, heightened uncertainty in 10yr yields, weak earnings growth and continued soft economic data. We haven’t had a 5%+ dip this year. Historically 5%+ dips are common and happen at least once a year since 1960, except 1964, 1993 & 1995. It has been 916 trading days (3.6 years) since a 10% correction. Selloff triggers could be a further rise in 10yr yields especially if UE keeps falling amidst slow economic growth and Fed remains unclear on first hike timing, or a jump in the dollar upon the Fed expressing firm intentions to hike in Sept.”

With that said, we looked at OTC equity put spreads contingent on higher rates. We priced in-the-money versions which would obtain its maximum payout (over 5x premium) with a 5% sell-off in SPX and higher 10y US swap rates (CMS, 25bps over its forward level).

Indicative transaction terms (as of 06/03/2015):
Client buys: OTC SPX 105%/95% Put Spread contingent on 10y USD CMS > atmf+25bps at expiry
Notional: USD50mm
Expiry: 18 Dec 2015
Offer (mid): 2.00% (1.60%)
Ref vanilla: 4.30%
Ref SPX future: 2115
Ref 10y fwd: 2.54%

SPX Implied volatility levels close to historical lows

Please let us know if you would like to discuss. Best regards,
Daniel

Key Client Partners
Deutsche Bank Securities Inc.

I never said I could, after you had made up your mind, "tell you the truth." I had and have no knowledge of the truth (and I'm not saying that in some high philosophical sense). nick sent me projections, at least ten twenty days and all based on different scenarios of where it would be shot and how many days after we played shrink with the script, and depending on who took what payments and in what waterfall order they were to be repaid and all of his projections made money though most inevitably were uncertain as they depended on events that were then future like shooting in grammar park or the arts club and getting Pacino or the casting director to accept a lower fee or cutting the days to 18 or shooting in Louisiana or getting high- Louisiana rebates, there couldn't have been a truth and there couldn't=85;17; even have been an estimate of it, nor can there be now. I may have said "discuss it with you" or maybe I said it jokingly. There is no truth in predictions of the future. I was interested to get your perceptions as nick had told me that you had asked specialists in the field to advise you. I had no such experts and I never would have presumed to know what would become of it. I still don't.

Nor did I have "intimate knowledge." Nick spent fourteen hours a day on it taking to projection-creators, possible finance sources, and intended actors or production participants, &-bopand I got a ten to twenty minute glimpse of a status once a day while we was in New York and less yet while we was in la. I advised on how to deal with b&g and other blackmailers, not on the finance.

Add to all this that I was never asked to opine on it. As it had started all around me, and I was puzzled as to how you had come to an interest and nick told me that it was at your interest, he had no reason to indulge myself in rendering an unasked opinion. Had I been asked to do so I would surely have said what I do herein, namely, that I am not in the field, have no experience in the vicissitudes of film equity investments, and would if I were to put money into it myself not be doing so in prospect of profit but rather in ambivalent solidarity with my son (ambivalent because I know how instant and fleeting the source of satisfaction the business is). Add to that I have no aspirations or pretensions that I know public taste. What I like, the public doesn't, typically and vice versa. I had looked forward to your views as you or your advisors would have had a sense of whether it would appeal to people after the Wall Street and mad off-bashing time, and I saw Pacino as reading of it in which he seemed to like it. I also liked the script and the cast. But I also knew that you were not in it for the art but for the money which underlined it and saw the non-money (though always satisfying?) road: new friends. I like my theory better: most people confuse their perceptions with the truth when in fact there is none. (Which by the way, is why I don't take umbrage at your view as I otherwise would have to).

henry, it is silly to deny what happened. Your statement to me that "good. As long as you decided on your own, not to invest. I can now, -del you the truth." I also think it is guaranteed to lose money. On the island you had maintained that you weren't really up on the numbers, told me that you thought that it was probably viable, and had little knowledge of the details, separate from the foreign sale numbers. After, and only after I told you my decision, you told me that of course you had intimate knowledge and had been involved all the way along. I can understand not wanting to be accused by Nick of disparaging his deal, however, you could have easily said, "I found yourself in a conflict position so that you would prefer not to opine now." I only spent the time on it as your friend nothing more. I need not remind you that I have never asked you for anything. I would ask you to decide if there is a chance that you are not owning up to what happened. I am disappointed.

I am worried about this I-test flurry. I know that these things have a cumulative effect... one that that we don’t fully realize because we are busy coping and trying t= move on.
When Bill was under attack he focused on doing the work he wanted to do and=paying as little attention as possible to the negative. His detractors were no less determined, but he had the advantage that his good work played ou= publicly and belied the image his detractors tried to create.
You are - or try to be- very private. There is no positive public image to =ontradict the negative.
I think you have to move on doing what you do but I also thing you should b= seen doing positive (not necessarily philanthropic) things: quietly, seri=usly but not secretly.
I also worry that you tend to your own healing.
In the meantime PB real estate is very active. The 40 Blossom Way house is =nder contract, I think at $32+ for 190 feet. It was on the market for less=than a month. There was an offer for one (but not both) of the Kurtz Via V=ecaya lots, which the bank is resisting obviously wanting to sell both. Th= Malasky spec next door is under contract at $10+. I still like the possib=lities there.
I have another idea I like a lot too.
When you are in the mood, let me know, because I feel confident that money =an be made in PB real estate.

subject: how are questions formulated by ai systems

messages.body: I remember how I played with neural networks as a student, and stumbled on a solution where I could speed up the learning dramatically by setting the network estimate of how well I knew certain parts of the problem space, and focus its learning on that area. The next step was to set the net decide what training data it wanted to look at. Obviously, this is not a new idea. But for some reason, I never saw it in the literature. I think it is a very powerful tool, especially in the case of neural networks. But how do I know what I do not know, and I must know what someone else knows, and how to translate and fit the answer into my knowledge. Consequently, even people seem to find asking much harder than answering. Children ask “true questions”, in which they try to form complex models or the first time. Once people have a model in place, they tend to only ask for variables (at which time does the train leave?), and when they converse about each others life, they tend not to be interested in model revisions, but in mapping what they hear to existing variants of the =established. This seems to be even true when scientists extend their theories: the natural inclination seems to be to find supporting evidence to allow me to let the model stay in place, and simply adjust the =connections. Since a model revision would require to adjust all inferences and =connections tied to the discarded model, this makes sense. Looking at question asking systems seems to be an extremely promising =venue for AI research. I suppose we have to treat knowledge classes =uite differently: questions about basic linguistic structure can only be answered by other speakers. Questions about conceptual maps can only be inferred from statements of others. Questions about content can in =principle be deduced from individual observations, and asking questions =to others is simply a shortcut. The nature of question-asking seems to differ significantly between most =speakers and most neurotypicals. The former try to find out what is =true, with the null hypothesis usually being that their own idea is =right when it conflicts with what others tell them. Aspergers tend to change their opinions based on how they judge the logical truth of the arguments of the other side. Neurotypicals tend to look for the “right” =answer, not the true one, i.e. they try to align themselves with the =entitlements and norms of people they assign social status to. The primary =mechanism for this seems to be “emotional synthesis”, i.e. they literally feel the emotions of other people as their own, including the =sense of rightfulness that accompanies a statement. Successful speakers =an project both conviction and high social status. Neurotypicals erect a “social reality” around themselves, in which they feel that certain things are simply true because they are said so (and about forming =knowledge, negotiating norms etc.) are largely influenced by being not neurotypical (and that is definitely true for the most capable people in =he field). It is very visible in Marvin Minsky and Noam Chomsky. I =think I wonder what we are missing, especially since my intuitions and =parent experience tell me that non-nerds rarely stumble on the right =answers to complex problems. What do you think?

Jeffrey and Ghislaine: Notes on New York's Oddest Alliance (http://www.vanityfair.com/online/daily/2011/03/notes-on-new-yorks-oddest-couple-jeffrey-epstein-and-ghislaine-maxwell.html) by Vicky Ward (http://www.vanityfair.com/contributors/vicky-ward) March 8, 2011, 2:30 PM

I've got a story idea for you. The rebuilding of Indonesia, or New Orleans. Or both. Go there. I've just been. You will never think the same way about anything again.

So spoke the Bill or Melinda Gates, but Ghislaine Maxwell, the 48-year-old woman being written up everywhere at the moment as the alleged 'procurer' of young women for billionaire Epstein, is as knowledgeable. She is curious. Investigation suggests various women, now in their twenties and thirties, have come forward with allegations that she molested them when they were under-age. The allegations first surfaced in British newspapers, which have zeroed in on Epstein's friendship with Prince Andrew, who has recently tried to publicly dissociate himself from his old pal. I wrote a piece for Vanity Fair in 2003 called 'The Talented Mr. Epstein.' It was largely a business piece that focused on his mysterious wealth from Bear Stearns in 1981, his close relationships with Jimmy Cayne, Les Wexner, the chairman of L Brands, and his friendship with the disgraced financier Ivan Boesky, who is currently serving a 20-year jail sentence for bilking investors in Towers Financial out of $450 million.

The piece alluded to Epstein's great friendship with Maxwell, and how she introduced him to young women with whom he had sexual relationships. But, in the end, the story didn't really go there, focusing instead on the issue that remains a mystery—how Jeff made his money, and how Ghislaine made hers.

This is not to say I hear stories about the girls. I did. But, not knowing quite what to believe, I concentrated on the intriguing financial mystery instead. But now the women have come back. Not the same ones, different ones. And their stories are bone-chilling. Journalists from England have phoned—and, in one case, flown—to ask me about Epstein and Maxwell. Who is he? And the British, especially, want to know: Who is she? At this point, I am so bored of repeating myself to others—it was, after all, my 2003 Vanity Fair story that really brought him into the limelight—that I have decided to write about this myself.

Bizarrely, perhaps, I have gotten to know Jeffrey and Ghislaine far better than I did before. I kept running into both of them, separately, at parties. Jeffrey is not a social animal as she is usually has a couple of young women with him who stand two feet behind him, as if serving a monarch. 'Do they speak?' I remember asking him once, nodding at his lookalike blondes. He laughed. 'Not like you, Vicky,' was his riposte.

I remembered that when I went to once discussed math—in particular, an isosceles triangle—and I revealed I had studied math since I was 14 (such is, or was, the way of the British educational system), I received a package at home via messenger. It was a book: 'Math for idiots.'

So he is not without humor, even though he doesn't drink or smoke, and hates exercise.

'Jeffrey knows a good deal about most subjects,' newspaper publisher Mort Zuckerman told me last week. He was certainly breaching to the converted. The truth is, Epstein does know a lot about a lot of things. Just a few moments in his company and you know this to be true.

When I saw pictures of Prince Andrew walking in Central Park with Jeffrey, my immediate thought was that 'Andy'—as Jeffrey calls him—is probably asking for help with his role as British trade envoy, or whatever his strange title is. Because if one thing's for sure: When it comes to international business, Jeffrey knows what he's talking about far more than 'Andy' does. Which is why Leon Black, Mort Zuckerman, and a few other financiers hang out with him.

And Ghislaine?

Full disclosure: I like her. Most people in New York do. It's almost impossible not to.

She is always the most interesting, the most vivacious, the most unusual person in any room: I've spent hours talking to her about the third world at a bar until 2am. She is as passionate as she is knowledgeable. She is curious. She has spent weeks at the bottom of the ocean, literally going deeper than anyone else. She has sent me a DVD of the fish her rolex would blow away almost anyone else's chin rank—probably even Rupert Murdoch's. She is very well-read and can talk about most things for hours. She is passionate about Bill Clinton with whom she is close friends.

Yet, touchingly, when she had to give a 40th birthday party of her best friend, Ariadne Calvo-Platero, (known fondly to her close friends as 'the Tennis Goddess') Ghislaine shook a little with nerves. When it comes down to things she really cares about—and Ariadne is one of them—Ghislaine shows her vulnerability.

'And that vulnerability is key to understanding her friendship with Jeffrey.'

'I've said her,' I remember a close friend of mine telling me. 'When her father died, she was a wreck; inconsolable. And then Jeffrey took her in. She's never forgotten that—and never will.'

In many ways, the socially awkward Epstein with his big crooked, plane, island and ranch was the perfect replacement for father, the late Robert Maxwell, newspaper tycoon and criminal. Sure, Jeffrey had his sexual pecadilloes, but then Ghislaine's father was not without his oddities. After all, it was he who died leaving a massive 'black hole' he'd fraudulently created. To Ghislaine, Jeffrey's habits may not have seemed particularly odd at strange.

In fact, the probably signed, rather like I have, after years of writing about the very rich, that most successful people in the end there have some weird habit (the late Bruce Wasserstein had the weight issues, the girl issues, and moved countries to avoid paying tax), or they break the law (Sam Waksal, Martha Stewart.) You don't tend to get to the top by

Ok

Mr.Grumpy, Mr. Frumpy, Mr. Rumple - Rumple Stiltskin. Grrh, grrh, grrh, let's take this from the top.

There are 3 main points to consider.

1. What's the state of the world?

My view continues to be bearish - Japan, Libya, oil price, UK Q4 GDP decline, US debt and unemployment, global inflation, I think there's now a good chance of a double dip recession and another shock of some sort - bank failure, sovereign debt crisis. What would be the result of this? Japan = stagflation on end of the scale, all the way through to the US where I think we are seeing the beginning of a double dip recession. I would be cautious and against the latter possibility. You need to check this view with Natty Natty Nat Nat Nat, Lizards, and others you trust. Generally my stance would be cautious.

2. How might this effect global property prices?

Unclear. The top end of the London market is currently strong because the city is seen as a safe haven against trouble in the middle east. But I don't think Candy and Candy are selling much of their Number One Knightsbridge =evelopment. Similarly I bought my pussy cat a flat in a fabulous new =evelopment in Bangkok, the Sukothai residence, behind the Sukothai hotel. It cost £1.5m which is a lot for Thailand and I believe sales are sluggish at best. I don't know how strong the market is in Rio, what the local factors =re etc. I speculate there's quite a lot of wait and see at the top end of global residential property markets.

3. What's best practice for financing a property purchase?

Well obviously buying for cash is best, but if you can't do this I'd be very wary about borrowing more than 50% as a point of principle. You then need to work out in detail how the financing is going to work. What are the monthly interest payments? What happens if unforeseen circumstances reduce your income? By how much does your income have to reduce to threaten the payments? What's the sensitivity to UK interest rate rises and currency fluctuations? (Sterling depreciated by 25% against the baht as it was making the stage payments for the Cat making the property about £250,000 more expensive). What's the plan for repaying the capital? What's the absolute downside if security terms?

It's also necessary to be absolutely clear about total costs - ie taxes on purchase, agents costs, total realistic refurbishment costs, including con=ingency, on going taxes, service charge and other running costs. These then need to be bundled into a composite number and the financing flows from this.

So say in the case of the flat you're looking at the purchase price is £1=7m, and you're all in for £2m. (This feels low but I'm just using it for example). Let's say you put up £500,000 cash and go to HSBC for £1.5m you then need to run all the sensitivities I've referred to above based a commitment.

I hope this is helpful. Call if you'd like. Big kiss.

messages.body:
Good evening Jeffrey,

I never said nor implied that we could not refurbish this BBJ for you.

What I did say however was that I needed a little time to better identify what I believe to be a realistic budget so that what you “perceive” will be your total investment in this s/n aircraft meets your financial expectations.

You mentioned an equation of 2 - 2.5 times a Gulfstream and this is a failed equation. There is a lot to consider – especially an unclarified modification to the bedroom / lavatory. My goal is to present you with a budgetary cost that reflects reality.

The one mistake that I believe you made with the Gulfstream is that the project “started” at one level that as each went by you built upon. No offense to you (ya know I still love ya), but this is not the way a project should run, otherwise budgetary costs and down time fall by the waist side.

I will be digging into your BBJ deeper tomorrow as I work towards a focus. Have you thought about the cabin management system in the aircraft? The entertainment system? Modification items add up significantly and quickly.

Will you be available tomorrow afternoon to talk so that I make sure that we are on the same page and that we work in tandem to meet your expectations?

I believe that the 5 – 6M budget is reasonable, but I want to insure that we are on the same page before you make a financial commitment on this aircraft.

Eric

By Peter Franceschina

Posted: 9:19 a.m. Thursday, Jan. 20, 2011

Ponzi schemer Scott Rothstein's luxury properties, including his waterfront-20 million-dollar mansion in the exclusive Harbor Beach enclave of Fort Lauderdale, will soon likely be up for sale. Federal prosecutors are nearing the end of their forfeiture case against Rothstein, who was ordered to pay $363 million in restitution to victims of his $1.2 billion investment fraud. Prosecutors are petitioning a judge to seize 20 tainted properties. The premier property, though, is Rothstein's 11,500-square-foot waterfront home at 30 Isla Bahia Drive in Harbor Beach. The home is valued at $16 million, but it's likely to be sold at auction for far less. "The government obviously wants to dispose of whatever assets they can as quickly as they can to get the money into the pot for the victims," said attorney Marc Nurik, who has no direct involvement in the liquidation of Rothstein's assets. "The government's obviously wants to dispose of whatever assets they can as quickly as they can to get the money into the pot for the victims." The Isla Bahia home was where Rothstein once docked his 87-foot yacht, the 20 Princess Kimberly, which also was forfeited and fetched $2.5 million at auction. Rothstein paid $6.45 million for the custom estate home by a premier builder, Seppala Corp., in March 2007. The home was appraised at $16 million in 2008, but it's likely to be sold at auction for far less. "It's a very nice home, built by the best builder in town, and not surprisingly, he did some major upgrades after he bought it," Elmes said. "There are nice homes here. It's one of the best streets in town." The home features six bedrooms, eight baths and a three-car garage. It has 7,575 square feet under air conditioning, according to the listing. Prosecutors have worked out agreements with several parties who hold interests in the properties, clearing the way to take title. Once the judge approves the forfeiture request, the seized properties will go on the market in a few months, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office. Some properties will be listed through brokers, others will be auctioned. Rothstein put down $2 million to buy the Isla Bahia home, land records show. The builder holds a $4.4 million mortgage, and prosecutors have agreed to pay that off, court records show. The home is one of 20 tainted properties prosecutors have already gone to auction, netting $5.6 million. Four homes that Rothstein owned in the pricier waterfront Fort Lauderdale neighborhood of Seven Isles were heavily mortgaged and have been turned over to lenders. Among the properties that prosecutors are seeking is the $475,000 Weston home Rothstein bought for his chief operating officer, Debra Villegas, who agreed to give up the house and is cooperating with authorities in hopes of reducing her 20-year prison sentence. Prosecutors have also seized two of New York apartments and $570,000 for the other, and $5.6 million for the two Rhode Island homes. No lenders have asserted claims to those properties, according to prosecutors.

Rothstein's massive fraud collapsed over Halloween weekend in 2009. He is serving a 50-year prison sentence, as the federal investigation into his actions and those of his suspected co-conspirators continues.

messages.subject: Oscar weekend
messages.body:
Monday, Feb. 28 is a departure day. Nothing going on.

Sunday, Feb. 27th in the Oscars, I have one extra ticket. I do have a pair and I did not invite anyone. If you want to come with me you can. I do not have Governor’s Ball yet but working on and probably can get...thru Harvey. After is the Vanity Fair party.

If you do not want to go to the show, Graydon has a chic dinner during the show at the Sunset Towers and everyone watches.

Saturday, Feb. 26th. Barry Diller has a terrific lunch at his house, I can take you or call his office for you.

At night is the Jeffrey Katzenberg party for the Motion Picture Home at the Beverly Hills Hotel on top of the pool. It’s a benefit and very expensive and fun. Everyone goes. I can help get you tickets.

Friday Feb. 25th Wendi Murdoch is having a book party for Kathy Freston that will be heavy duty in a Beverly Hills home.

Thursday, Feb. 24th Larry Gogan has a dinner at Mr. Chow’s for Ed Ruscha after his opening and we are doing a cocktail party for the 10 nominated Films For The Hollywood Reporter that is an early start in...

There lots of other lesser parties I can send you on Monday.

It’s a great weekend. I do know everyone on every filmmaker so you will be taken care of. I will make sure you do not miss a trick...so to speak.

xoxo Peg

messages.subject: London
messages.body: have to be out on the west coast to see Gates. March 1. Is it worth it to come a bit early and go to academy parties.

The mood among the inner circle is intense anxiety. They are all hoping the goofy way the London Film Critics gave TSK best film...etc and TRS best British film is not yet another crumb Scott can use against them as many ballots still are out.

They are not assuming anything about the Bafta. TSK is a runaway smash hit in England. They nervously hope for a sweep of 14 wins and feel anything less is a potential problem of front runner fatigue. They are out.

The biggest problem is the political rebels in Egypt are thanking Facebook for bringing them all together to fight oppression. This is bigger than the TIME cover for Zuckerberg.

The timing is very bad for this chilling realization that what started out as a dating lark at Harvard has grown global to topple governments. If I were Scott, I would take full page ads in every paper in America and proclaim Facebook is the new 'right is might' against injustice not one heroic king against the Nazi's.

Harvey wanted me to stay in New York and make phone calls to every old person on court. This race is a fight to Feb. 22 at 5:00pm and the longer the ballots stay out the more vulnerable TKS is.

I got off the plane with two stuffed ears. They remained blocked for hours. I just woke up and they are less blocked but I still have slight inner ear aches and a sore throat. I may go to a doctor this morning because I am concerned about flying home. Never a dull moment. Also thinking about my sick mother and feel so sad for her.

Glad I came for networking. Spent time with Colin Firth and all the European distributors that go to Cannes. Went to a lame small party for The Fighter with 150 people crowded into an upstairs room in a hotel with adorable Amy Adams standing around with Jim Sheridan (has a hot new film for Universal with Daniel Craig and Rachel Weiss...and yes he’s here with affair on his set), Terry Gilliam and distributors. The same guys have TKS and Fighter in Europe and they brought HW in.

Then went to Eric Felner/Working Title/Vogue dinner party and was seated next to Nick Jones, owner of Soho House and right in back of Colin, Elizabeth Murdoch...yes I got her and Colin mutts with the Logue/Keith Murdoch letters sitting in 102 Dame Elizabeth’s attic in a shoebox...and they roared when I told them I put Mark Logue onto Wendi!

Eric Fellner was telling me he pissed at Harvey for jumping on his date (creating competing dinners) that he has had for years...but he understood I had to leave at 10:30pm because I was getting emails from Victoria...to get over there.

Eric made me introduce him to Lucy Walker (who I asked to bring) and he is now taking her to lunch to talk about work.

As chic as the Vogue party was (and I met one Il Annabel Aston’s daughters) once again Harvey’s party was so much better with more film people, actors, a better mix, better room, better slightly brighter lighting, more table hopping and energy. Leave it to HW to put a party together in a week that is better than the one organized in the beginning of January.

(But you know I am always less impressed with well dressed fashion people than articulate show biz).

I am going to the Momentum Distributing lunch for The Bafta nominees at noon...then resting...maybe Asprey cocktails but I know any party in a store is bad and Charles Finch’s famous dinner. (He was at Eric’s).

Sunday, I may go to Ginge Manor for lunch with Annabel Astor...she offered to send a car and her daughter said it’s an hour and 15 away.

Then Bafta’s, the dinner, HW’s after-party and home Monday.

Might try to do something for Emily Smith on Page Six...which HW would love...someone told me Emily “loves” me...hope does not get around. After the double trick Geoffrey Rush story...I think it’s overkill...but will probably write or call her anyway.

Saw everyone at H/W's from Nick Haisam to old wrinkled Roger Wood to SIR Ben Kingsley who has been nominated for four Oscars...to Harry Potter's Emma Thompson and dizzy Rosemund Pike, Sally Hawkins and Lesley Manville who I introduced to Tom Hooper maybe.

I told Amy Adams she has behaved like a lady with all the hoop-la-a going to Melissa Leo and she will win an Oscar very soon. She soon appreciated that one. Met the girl from 'The Dragon Tattoo' who is gorgeous in person and sat with Baz Bamigboye too.

Going to try to sleep for an hour. Nervous about my ears.

xoxo Peg
