messages.subject: Customs
messages.body:
Jeffrey,

Each Customs office requires different procedures for clearing in,
For instance Teterboro sometimes requires a fax copy of EAPIS form which would include passenger info: Name, DOB, Passport #, all info included on EAPIS form, even yesterday when I first spoke to officer “RR” he first stated, did you Fax a Gen Dec, I told him, I filed EAPIS and we also are PreClearing customs in STT, that point, he informed me to just bring my stamped GenDec to his office after I unload my passengers at Meridian. Secondly, we have to give “Notice of Arrival” to customs at least one hour prior to our arrival, Eileen received her phone call from Latin Customs agent Officer Goico at 6:05pm just 1 hour before our arrival. I can only assume that Officer Goico didn’t think I gave notice of Arrival, so he tried calling my phone, she did not leave a Voice mail either, so she must have called my emergency contact on my EAPIS form which was Eileen’s cell number.

Nothing is standard for Customs arrivals, between PBJ, STT and TEB, each require different paperwork, STT requires, EAPIS, phone call Notice of arrival, copies of aircraft registration, Pilots medical, and 3 copies of Gen Dec. PBJ requires EAPIS, only a phone call to their office for Notice of Arrival, no other paper work required. TEB requires EAPIS, phone call for notice of arrival, sometime requires a Fax copy of Gen Dec.

The Physics of the Universe Summit

Hosted at SpaceX, Caltech and the Andaz West Hollywood Hyatt, January 8,9,10 2010

To accomplish the extraordinary, you must seek extraordinary people. -- James Lee Byars

In this two day retreat we hope to bring together the top minds (thinkers and doers) in the fields of the physics of the universe both theoretical and experimental. We want to ask and answer questions like "How much can we understand about the universe, soon?" "What is the role of theory and of experiment in getting there?" "Are there things we may not understand?" and "How much of the universe is knowable?" We will have a moderated discussion and we are convinced that when the best people talk we can standard prepared talks, and focus on exciting forefront issues, where there may be differences of opinion, or new results that will stimulate wide discussion. You will receive more information about the program and your own possible role in the near future. The summit is inspired by the onset of the Large Hadron Collider, the Planck mission, the recent results by satellite and ground based experiments on dark matter searches, and the vast progress in theory. Also to meetings such as the LHC Olympics, and the workshops of the past years at the MCTP, KITP and Perimeter as well as interdisciplinary gatherings of the ASU Origins, the Edge Master-Classes and Google's SciFoo.

Venues/Highlights:
1. The first day of the summit will be held at the headquarters of SpaceX <http://www.spacex.com>. The end of the day will be marked by Elon Musk giving a tour of his "Falcon" rocket and "Dragon" construction and missions. A Tesla surprise will be built into the tour.
2. The second day will be held at Caltech's Cahill Center <http://sustainability.caltech.edu/LEED/NewConstruction/Cahill> for talks and discussion.
3. Participants will be housed at The Andaz West Hollywood <http://westhollywood.hyatt.com/hyatt/hotels/index.jsp?Hyatt=hollywood>
4. The kick-off reception and dinner will be given, sponsored by Nick Pritzker.
5. The evening of the first meeting will be a premiere of a short film by Jesse Dylan <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Dylan> on the LHC.

The summit is by invitation only. There is no registration or other fees; just make your way to LA and the rest is covered (limited air travel support will be available for younger participants).

Invited Participants include: Steven Weinberg, Mathew Buckley, Frank Wilczek, Neil Weiner, Savvas Kousios, Liantao Wang, Cumrun Vafa, Nima Arkani-Hamed, Aaron Pierce, Lisa Randall, David Gross, Gordy Kane, Joe Lykken, Kip Thorne, Chiara Nappi, Edward Witten, Gia Dvali, John Schwarz, Nati Seiberg, Mike Turner, Rocky Kolb, David Politzer, Lawrence Krauss, Steve Myers, Barry Barish, Hiroshi Ooguri, Marc Kamionkowski, Stephen Hawking, Mark Wise, Andrew Lange, Roger Blandford, Sunil Golwala, Sean Carroll, John Preskill, Fabiola Gianotti, Laura Baudis, David Saltzberg, Asimina Arvanitaki, Kathryn Zurek, Mirko Boezio, and others (to be ordered alphabetically).

messages.subject: Kurtzer article in NY Daily News
messages.body:
Dear friends,

Following is an op-ed that appeared in today's NY Daily News B All the best B Dan

Opinion

The border between reality and politics: What's new and what's not in Obama's stance on '67 border

BY
Daniel Kurtzer

Sunday, May 22 2011

In His

Middle East speech last week,
President Obama argued forcefully for Israeli-Palestinian peace, emphasizing
unshakeable
U.S. support for
Israel and the need for an outcome that results in two states: Israel and a sovereign,
contiguous Palestinian state. The President's speech, and the 1967 lines as referenced by and
simmered through incremental change, while avoiding grand plans and big strategies.

Yet already, the remarks have become deeply controversial.

The President's reference to the 1967 lines, and Obama three times 'under the bus.' Former
Arizona Gov. Mike Huckabee said, 'President Obama has betrayed Israel.' A statement by the
Simon Wiesenthal Center referred to the 1967 lines as 'the Auschwitz borders.'
Widespread Israelis in Israeli's entourage said Obama didn't understand Israel and its situation.

A nasty U.S.-Israel spat is erupted. It was led bare in the unusually blunt remarks made by Netanyahu after meeting Obama on Friday, and it centers to impact both the
peace process and the U.S.-Israel relationship. The American Jewish Public Affairs Committee and Netanyahu's address to Congress tomorrow?

What are we to make of the heated rhetoric in the wake of Obama's remarks? Is this about reality, politics or a bit of both? Was Obama's
previous U.S. policy or rather an incremental step forward?

First, a brief primer on a very complicated subject. Before 1967, the dividing line between Israel and the
West Bank was the Armistice Line, negotiated between Israel and Jordan in 1949. Subsequently, Jordan annexed the West Bank but renounced its claim to that territory in 1988.

Israel occupied this territory in the 1967 war. Since the
Madrid peace conference in 1991, Israel and the Palestinians have been negotiating the details of the transfer of these territories to the
Palestinians. The expectation has been that Palestine would set up an independent state, and Israel's security requirements would be addressed.

Meanwhile, over the course of the last few peace talks, Israel has built settlements in the West Bank, (lower settlements in the
Jordan Valley. Israel from Egyptian control in 1967, where are unilaterally be transferred to the Palestinians.) About 300,000 Israeli settlers

Hi, Captain!
How was Europe? I said you were coming back home today. Did you hear about my crazy flight last night?
So one of the cross country guys I flew with had school had to deliver a C127 from Tuba to Miami to someone who just bought it and he offered me to fly it from the right seat and log a lot of old flight time in a day. So I went to Tulsa yesterday morning to pick it up. The plane was fine and even though it just came out of annual, the alternator malfunctioned and failed on our last leg in the middle of the night somewhere over the Everglades.
A few uneventful legs during the day, we took off with full tanks at Tallahassee yesterday evening. We planned to top off again in Gainesville so we make it to KOPF with a nice reserve. But GNV weather deteriorated quickly after we took off and went to 400ceilings. The other guy was flying this leg and wanted to shoot an approach and try landing. We went to minimums, didn't break out of the clouds, we missed and decided to leave and continue on our way south. He wanted to just keep going all the way to Opa Locka. There was a good chance we would have had enough fuel but the reserve would have been questionable. I was thinking about turning around and going back to GNV and try to land. I was thinking about the single engine plane in the middle of the night thinking about our trip starting to sound like a bad idea and refuel first. He let me get the controls and take it into Lakeland to top off again and I glad we did. Thinking back, we probably should have stopped there for the night. Maybe an hour after leaving KLAL in level flight, without warning, the whole plane went dark. I was flying, we were on IFR flight plan when we lost all cons, lights, transponder. Everything. I declared an emergency and was vectored to KOPF. We were given a time to tell center what was going on and they told us to keep going to KOPF, descend at our discretion if we lost everything again, do an ILS to 30 and then call them to cancel our IFR. I really need to get one.
I was trying to decide whether to keep the controls for the approach or give to the other guy. I thought he knew how to work his 696 better and could set me up but we weren't doing so well with the clouds and I kept flying from my seat and had him shine a light on my instruments and work the gps. Weather was not too bad but still ifr with 700ceilings in Opa Locka. We were able to get the power back a few times before for landing but always just for a moment. I had to shoot an ILS with a garmin flying from the right seat, in the dark. The unexpected part was not being able to turn on the runway lights with the radios dead. Tower was closed, the flaps are also electric, we descended through clouds and couldn't find the runway it was too late to make a safe landing. I went around, got very pale and trying not to get back into the clouds, came in again. Once I landed and cleared the runway, I could barely taxi it back my legs were shaking so hard.
Then I put the newspaper down, stopped doing my nails :) and went straight to MIA to take a flight home. I am still in disbelief.
Frightened Lima
Sent via BlackBerry by AT&T

messages.subject: thoughts
messages.body:
My guess is, as you see this long letter, you are tempted to skim through, quickly find the point, see what I want from you and move on. You won't find it. This is not a plea. It's more of a revelation and there is a lot to digest. I have been slowly making notes for months so there is no sense of urgency and I hope you can find a moment of peace to really read the words and know they are sincere.

I want to start by saying I am grateful for you being a part of my life throughout the years. I also feel extremely lucky to have been able to do what I'd done during the past six months. I wish you too had the luxury of being able to leave behind everything and every day know, deep outside of the cushy cotton room and try living a completely new and different life. It has been a wild ride and I am in awe of the outcome.

For over a year, you have disciplined me to not say anything you were not yourself. Although you didn't have the tools to fix the problem, you were able to help me identify it. Meanwhile, it never occurred to me how far from the truth I had strayed. I had been able to identify the emails I sent you, without cringing. I had been able to let it go far and really embraced it.

I really imagine your frustration and hope you will end your day forgiving me for so ignorantly pushing the limits of your love and patience. I believe you did your best trying to open my eyes. I vividly remember you telling me I would realize this one day when I did. I do not want to do it want you to find that time. I was tough to know about, even though some are not fun for me to share.

During the first few months when something happened that proved your point, I couldn't help thinking you had been right all along. I was slowly stopping expecting you to have all the answers. I had to use behind the door and I was slowly stopping to expect you to have all those little tricks. I had watched you use over the years. I always knew you were smart but after closely examining some of your advice and strategies, I don't know how you have the patience to live among normal people. The advantages of getting things done with you are immense. I have been able to close the deal or the value of making people feel welcome and good about themselves is a firm approach to close the deal or the value of making people feel welcome and good about themselves is just a few of my favorites.

In light of full disclosure, I want to share some thoughts about my bad behavior in our relationship. I owe an apology to you and three of my confidants who labeled the problems correctly over the years. I must say again that I never intentionally deceived you. I was much too stubborn to admit these things even to myself at the time. I absolutely believed I was the best girl you could find. However, my behavior did not even closely resemble the person I thought myself to be.

The fact is got spoiled. But it is not the maids, chefs or drivers that I miss. I look for granted being waited on and exposed to great minds, instead I chose to focus on the small great and that's a shame. While I have been able to do many things, I have not been able to make people feel welcome and good about themselves. There are so many questions I wish I had asked when I had the opportunity.

I also blamed you for my insecurities. My body issues were more serious than you ever knew and feeling inadequate was indeed a big reason behind my jealousy and ridiculous demands. While it's no secret that helping girls get over their insecurities was never your forte, I aggravated the situation by putting that burden on you. I relied on you to make me feel good about myself when it was ultimately all in my control. As I am sure you know, I have been able to make myself feel good about myself and I am in control. The only way I know to get your full attention, although negative, for more than a few minutes. So picked stupid fights with you and blamed you for things that were ultimately my responsibility. I am sorry for that and I am admitting it to myself at last. But I don't want to do it again. I don't want you to find yourself in the same situation with someone else, so I am giving you the unvarnished truth as raw as it is. Although I had a few doubts, I decided to send this to you. I am having a while flag now because we were in fact right about most things. I recognize I am thankful for all the effort you put into trying to explain.

The process of getting to those realizations has been quite a journey. At first, I was just shocked that there was actually nothing to hide from you.

Later, I felt so embarrassed, I decided not to admit anything to you. I had been the crazy man on the streets yelling, with full conviction, about the end of the world. I think about how much you had to love me to live with him every day and I am so sorry you had to put up with it.

But now I think it's only fair you get the credit - because it's NOT too late!

I could have spent the rest of my life as that petty miserable brat that turned into and now I don't have to. That thought alone makes me so happy. I feel like I have the answers to almost everything I need in order to live a great life. In fact, I finding I learned so much from you, it is not really fair to other people.

I am again and it is such a pleasure to be able to say that I am content with myself. I am in the shape I always wanted to be. I love that I can feel and hold a conversation, or make a great sushi impression. I am actually choosing to talk to me, condone it, help me, spend time with them. Strangers start conversations with me, girls flirt with me. I am not kidding when I say I now get compliments about how I look and how I carry myself. I am not saying this to brag, but rather to illustrate the point that you are laughing in the corner somewhere. The fact is I took a long and practice to do what you can appreciate my fascination it worked. It may not seem very significant to you but I haven't experienced anything like a few months and I don't think I just became my ass giggles this. I can now get done what I need to.

During the holiday airport mess, I got stuck in Atlanta on my way home. At flights to anywhere in the northeast were sold out for days and I had number 200 on a standby list for a flight that was already full. People were sleeping on the floors. I didn't have my uniform. I managed to get moved to number 2 on the next flight home just by talking to the gate agents while others waited for a flight for 3 extra days. It was actually a lot of fun.

I still worry about certain things in my life and as you know there are a few stressful issues I need to sort out, but I can't think of the last time I let anyone run my day. There is a priceless. I could go on for pages but my point is, I am in a very peaceful happy place, which is a great extent a result of my experiences with you. I am grateful for the time we spent together after reading this letter. Because you have succeeded. I owe you for the greatest lesson in life. I miss you best friend but don't blame you for being angry and resentful. Spend all the time you want hating me but know that when you are done and you want a friend, I am here.

inadequate was indeed a big reason behind my jealousy and ridiculous demands. While it's no secret that helping girls get over their insecurities was never your forte, I aggravated the situation by putting that burden on you. I relied on you to make me feel good about myself when it was ultimately all in my control. As I am sure you know, I have always been my own worst critic and have said the most horrible and petty things, subconsciously knowing you would suddenly find time and talk to me. Unfortunately, it was the only way I knew to get your full attention, although negative, for more than a few minutes. So I picked stupid fights and said hurtful things, knowing you would come to my rescue and reassure me that everything was alright, admitting it to myself at all. But I don't want to do it again, nor do I want you to find yourself in the same situation with someone else, so I am giving you the unconditional truth as raw as it is. Although I had a few moments of weakness, I am actually doing quite well and am in a good place. I am finally at peace and have been for quite some time.
The process of getting to those realizations has been quite a journey. At first, I was just shocked that there was actually method in my madness.

Later, I felt so embarrassed, I decided not to admit anything to you. I had been the crazy man on the streets yelling, with full conviction, about the end of the world. I think about how much you had to love me to live with him every day and I am so sorry you had to put up with it.

But I think it's only fair you get the credit - because it's NOT too late! I could have spent the rest of my life as that petty miserable brat I had turned into and now I don't have to. That thought alone makes me so happy. I feel like I have the answers to almost everything I need in order to live a great life. In fact, I am finding I learned so much from you, it's not really fair to other people.

I am again and it is such a pleasure to be able to say that I am content with myself. I am in the shape I always wanted to be, I love that I can fly a jet and hold a conversation, or make a great Sasha impression. I have a job that I love and I am able to talk to me, confide in me, help me, invite me to spend time with them. Strangers start conversations with me, girls flirt with me. I am not kidding when I say I now get compliments about how happy I seem. I have even been told that I am like a breath of fresh air. People are laughing at the corner somewhere. I admit it takes an effort and practice but you can't appreciate my fascination that it worked. It may not seem very significant to you but I haven't experienced anything like it my whole life. I don't think it's just because my ass jiggles less. I can now get done what I need and have fun in the process.

During the holiday airport mess, I got stuck in Atlanta on my way home. All flights to anywhere in the northeast were sold out for day and I was number 200 on the standby list for a flight that was already full. People were sleeping on the floors. I didn't have my uniform. I managed to get moved to number 2 and on the next flight home just by talking to the gate agents while others waited for a flight for 3 extra days. You were actually there for me. It had been a long time since I had that kind of fun.

I still worry about certain things in my life and as you know there are a few stressful issues I need to sort out, but I can't think of the last time I let anyone run my day. That alone is priceless. I could go on for pages but I won't. I just wanted to let you know how much I appreciate you and how much you have helped me with you. I hope you can feel some sense of accomplishment after reading this letter, because you have succeeded. I owe you for the greatest lesson in my life.

I am aware I already crashed the airplane in the process. The truth is when you make that many bad decisions in the air, a controlled crash is sometimes the better option. I survived and I'm not flying into a wall. I am actually doing quite well and am in a good place. I am finally at peace and have been for quite some time. I don't even begin to cover what guilty I feel. I miss my best friend I don't blame you for being angry and resentful. Spend all the time you want hating me but know that when you are done and you want a friend, I was actually there. In the meantime I hope you stay happy.

Dear Jeffrey,

Hello. Happy New Years. I trust this note finds you well and that you had a great holiday break.

A few updates:

* I spoke with Eva about your giving the donation for enhanced education to my Center in <REDACTED> name. She knew about it of course already. Eva will discuss it with <REDACTED> to see if she wants to come to the Center to see what it is we do.

This also enables us to expand our weekly fellowship course (including developing more online materials) to teach the teachers: to educate residents, attendings and medical students in integrative approaches.

* Did you ever get a chance to look at the bacteriophage materials? Seem promising for new a antibiotic class

* How did your conversation about placebos with Ted Kaptchuk go? I got a cryptic email from him that it seemed "fine"

* Did you get an opportunity when you met with the Templeton Fdt to talk with them or give them the materials about proposals from CCHR for a study in spirituality and healthcare outcomes?

Let me know when you have gotten things stable with him and we can talk further about your health. I will ask him to send me notes (pending at the moment) to keep him in his loop also.

That's enough for now.

Here's to a healthy, successful and enjoyable 2011.

Best,

Woody

messages.subject: Good News: Statues Across The Third World. Bad News: Microsoft Forgotten
messages.body:
Gladwell: History Will Reveal Gates, Forget Jobs

Malcolm Gladwell has stirred up quite the controversy in tech circles with an off-the-cuff remark that history will remember Bill Gates fondly while Steve Jobs slips into obscurity.

Speaking at the Toronto Public Library's Appel last month, the author of The Tipping Point and Outliers likened Gates' charitable work to the German armaments maker Oskar Schindler's famous efforts to save his Jewish workers from the gas chambers during World War II.

'Gladwell, riffing on his idea that the entrepreneur is the main hero of the modern age, said that contrary to the current fascinations with the business successes of people like Gates and Jobs, future generations will remember them more for what they gave back to society than for how they went about enriching themselves.

Gates, who stepped down from his role as head of Microsoft several years ago to devote himself to the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and other charitable and advisory work, will be remembered as a giant among entrepreneurs, says Gladwell. Jobs, who is currently revered for co-founding Apple and then returning to the company to rescue it from irrelevance before his death with a series of hugely popular products like the iPhone and iPad, will be largely forgotten, the author said.

'Gates is a class act,' said Gladwell. 'He is the most ruthless capitalist. And then he decides, he wakes up one morning and he says, 'Enough.' And he steps down, he takes his money, takes it off the table ... and I think, I firmly believe that 50 years from now, he will be remembered for his charitable work. No one will even remember what Microsoft is.'

'And of the great entrepreneurs of this era, people will have forgotten Steve Jobs. Who's Steve Jobs again?

'But Gates, there will be statues of Gates across the Third World, and people will remember him as the man who ... you know, there's a reasonable shot, because of his money, we will cure malaria.'

What defines me most at this point in= life are my achievements: at 15, as well as attending school, I was playing tennis and going to Art School, at 17 I completed, simultaneously, Russian and British educational systems with great results and received an Art =chool Diploma (tennis had to give way to beauty sleep). At 20 I was working in the City of London and at 23 in New York on =Wall Street =855. Seems that living in the world's capitals has become my main hobby. Sounds pretty intimidating when I put it on paper, but I like to think that I have remained a fun and amiable person, open to meeting new people, exploring new places and new experience=. Beyond food, I love traveling - one of my favorite trips was backpacking across Vietnam, from Sagon to Hanoi with a best friend. Trying a fried silk worm was definitely a highlight, not a very pleasant one. Enjoy drawin= and the arts, from museums to ballet and opera to rock and house concerts and contemporary installations, and wish I had more time for it. Jeffrey, attached a word doc with data on scientific publications from Iran and Iraq: number of publications from 2000-2009, how often they are cited, and the h-index for authors. An h-index of X means the author has X publications cited at least X times each – a simple way to combine quantity and quality into a single number.

There are some pitfalls in interpreting this type of data. It includes any publication with one author from Iran/Iraq. Some of publications may have only minor contributions from there.

Some fields, like Math, Econ or Informatics, tend to be underrepresented because of the way how publishing works in these fields. A world-class mathematician might for example have problems to keep up with a medico clinic in terms of publication and citation counts. One can correct for such factors, but the optimal way depends on the objectives of the analysis.

Let me know whether these data are useful to you.

All the best,
Thomas

http://www.radaronline.com/ [1]t's -80 s hard to say goodbye when you're having fun!
Yes, I'm leaving my last PageSixLive.com/ [2] entry.
On Tuesday, I was the founding editor of Radar Online http://www.radaronline.com/ [3], one of the country's biggest celebrity websites.
The sandbox I get to play in now is a lot larger, and the gig often will take me to Los Angeles and Las Vegas and New York City.
But I love The Palm Beach Post http://www.pbpst.com/ [4] and the readers who supported me with comments, tips, and criticism for the past seven years with a heavy heart.
I love Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, and not just because it's my home. There are few places in this country as quirky as Pa<REDACTED> Beach, Stuart, Boca and Wellington. News people who work here know they're lucky because, indeed, there never is a dull moment.
For more, look below or click here.
My first story was a profile of the controversial Welli developer Glenn Straub, a West Virginia who conducts business like a pirate and who was attacked by a state attack coal veins.
The 2004 piece opened with an anecdote about how Straub was so reviled that polo fans cheered when he injured himself in a potentially fatal fall during a Palm Beach Polo Club game. Straub complained about the coverage a little, but I believe he secretly loved the attention.
I'll confess to a rough beginning in Palm Beach society a couple months later.
To some, including the recently deceased Dame Celia Lipton Farris http://www.palmbeachdailynews.com/society/celia-lipton-farris-a-great-dame-in-ever-1316465.html [4], a great philanthropist, I did not make out from head to toe at a party where I might have 20 appeared without a tie and a shave, she told me. I never got around to buying a blue blazer with gold buttons or loafers adorned with some crest.
Publicly, Palm Beach society didn't acknowledge PageSixLive.com. But secretly, I believe it loved the attention.
Some public officials, meanwhile, will welcome the news of my departure. The Palm Beach County Office http://www.pbso.org/ [5] half-kiddingly promised me lunch at the Palm Beach Yacht Club http://www.pbyc.com/ [6] if I left the Post.
I guess stories about on-duty sex, violence, incompetence and corruption at PBCSO was grating on the administration's nerves.
I'm told former West Palm Beach Mayor Lois Frankel, now a U.S. Congress hopeful, made a round of gleeful calls when she heard about PageSixLive's demise.
Good luck about that PageSixLive's demise.
The reader, the driving force behind PageSixLive.com, as unforgiving of spelling and grammar mistakes as the flaws of the characters I wrote about.
I've been subjected to a tough crowd, one as unforgiving of spelling and grammar mistakes as the flaws of the characters I wrote about.
You took the time to write more than 40,000 comments. Many were on the money and well crafted. Many were plain stupid or wrong. And some were obviously written by individuals guilty of BWI, blogging while impaired.
None, however, was dull. And every single one kept me on my toes.
There would have been very little content on this site without tipsters. You know who you are, even if many of you remained anonymous.
I'll miss you all, without one of you calling me or text messaging me with stories.
And for that, I couldn't thank you enough.
Because if there's one thing that a website editor fears the m=ost, it's having no fun.

strange. I will copy and paste:

I am very pleased to have this opportunity to recommend Alexa Staley to you. I first met her as one of the outstanding students in my class, Physics 104: Introductory Physics II, in her first year at Bowdoin. Since that time I have had the pleasure of watching her develop into a dedicated researcher and leader of our senior class physics students. Her strength of purpose and active intelligence are notable among our majors.

Alexa is quite serious about physics and began taking courses at the 300 level (namely, Methods of Theoretical Physics, the watered courses in our sequence for students that intend to major in physics). She has taken all of the 300 level courses that we offer and several theoretical courses that otherwise might have been skipped by her study away semester because of course sequencing issues. Her strong performance in both 200 and 300 level course work led to the award of the Hall Prize, our “most promising sophomore” prize, named for Bowdoin graduate and discoverer of the eponymous effect, Edwin Herbert Hall.

In the spring of her sophomore year Alexa was a student in my Statistical Mechanics course, Physics 229. This course has the reputation of being one of the more challenging in our major and is populated by physics majors in their junior and senior years. The course covers level theoretical physics and is relatively abstract and the mathematical reasoning strangely different from other physics applications. Alexa’s previous exposure to advanced mathematical methods was a clear asset. Her weakness, which is common to sophomores in the class, was a lack of experience with the physical applications of the formalism. Nonetheless, she did quite well in the course and illustrated solutions and would clearly communicate her ideas and questions in class and in private discussion. Her submitted solutions were always exemplary. Her A- reflects excellent mastery of the course material and steadily growing sophistication as a problem solver.

As Departmental Chair, I consulted closely with Alexa about her course choices for her junior year. She was highly committed to the University of Otago in New Zealand. She was highly committed to that challenge and to her physics studies. She chose to take a full load of physics courses. Thus, she deliberately chose to visit an English speaking country where advanced course work in Physics could be part of her program. We discussed the difference in course levels carefully, but for a variety of reasons, she ultimately chose an upper level Quantum and Atomic Physics course for which she had insufficient background. In response, she dove in and taught herself the material in the first chapters of Griffiths’ Quantum Mechanics textbook in a matter of weeks. Although her own report of this daunting experience tends to minimize her level of mastery, I cannot name more than a handful of students in my 15 years of teaching at Bowdoin that would embrace and excel at this challenge in the same amount of time. Her performance in this upper level course is a symptom of both her intellectual ambition and her work ethic. She has talent, works hard, and earns her success. I am sure that my colleague, Thomas Baumgart, who has supervised her senior honors thesis, will provide additional examples of her independence and drive. They have been distinguishing characteristics of her work.

In summary, Alexa will bring an unusual degree of commitment and excellent preparation for graduate work in physics to your program. She has more than the necessary talent, initiative and drive to succeed in a rigorous and research intensive program. I give her my highest recommendation: She will be an excellent scientist.

messages.subject: New release today
messages.body:
I'm excited to be able to tell you about a major new release day across our whole suite of products.

I began the development of our products nearly 30 years ago. When we released Mathematica in 1988 it transformed technical computing—but for us it just provided the base for three decades of amazing innovation. At the very beginning I defined principles which have continued to guide our development, and have led us to create a technology stack of unprecedented proportions, broadly spanning computation and knowledge.

Encompassing the breakthroughs of both Mathematica and Wolfram|Alpha, we've recently released the Wolfram Language, which defines a new approach to programming and computation. Today we're releasing a major upgrade to the Wolfram Language—further strengthening its core capabilities, and adding a host of major new areas.

Unlike other languages, the Wolfram Language is built to automate as much as possible, and to build in as much data about the world as possible. It elegantly combines many modern programming paradigms, as well as integrating the latest AI techniques, including many breakthroughs made at Wolfram Research.

Our products are available both for desktop and cloud (including private clouds). You can go to our Wolfram Open Cloud to check out the latest capabilities.

If you're interested in software development or research and development, go to: http://www.wolfram.com/development-platform

If you're interested in learning modern programming and computational thinking, go to: http://www.wolfram.com/ewl

And for our whole story, see: http://www.wolfram.com

I also posted a blog today about the latest release: http://blog.wolfram.com/2016/08/08/today-we-launch-version-11

The Wolfram Language is perhaps the largest and broadest integrated technology system ever built—and it's used in top organizations all over the world across every industry. In the past it's been strongest in R&D; today it's rapidly expanding into the deployment of large production systems.

I've personally been deeply involved in the design and architecture of our system throughout its evolution—and today I couldn't be more excited about the rate of innovation we've achieved, and the way in which we've been able to use our own technology to make this happen.

Particularly with the new release today, there are amazing opportunities opening up with the Wolfram Language. I hope you'll be able to take advantage of them. We'd be pleased to answer your questions—and we're also always happy to get your suggestions about how we can make our technology stack even more useful in your particular area.

Stephen Wolfram
Founder & CEO, Wolfram Research
Creator of Mathematica, Wolfram | Alpha and the Wolfram Language http://www.stephenwolfram.com

messages.subject: Topaz directorship
messages.body:
Can I ask your advice on something.

Before Xmas I was contacted by Linklaters and asked whether I would consider becoming a member of a new board for the soon to be IPOed company, Topaz. This is Oman-based, marine and other offshore oil and gas services company operating in Middle East and Caspian, seeking to grow in Africa and Brazil. It is owned by Renaissance Services, run by a wealthy family in Oman. I met the chairman, Samir, and fancy him a lot.

I have not decided on this. I am slightly concerned that a combination of growing Global Counsel and focussing on our clients needs plus my soon to be public Lazard role and senior advisor plus Glencore directorship all give me enough to be getting on with. On the other hand, Topaz will strengthen my networks.

Linlaters have come back and offered the following view:

What would this appointment do for PM and his consulting business?

Samir's view was this would be. Topaz is the first 'real' (ie genuine Middle Eastern) company coming to the London market, a geography that is teeming with potential waiting to break out and this would be creating a piece of history for the Middle East in the London market and you being associated with that should mean you can take some credit for this land-mark deal. It will raise your profile in the Middle East and the emerging markets and could raise other interesting opportunities for you and your consulting business. It will also put you on the board of shareholders that are listed on the website under the board of directors and shareholders.

Potentially of more interest to you and your consulting business might be the network of Samena Capital and I attach a link to their website.

http://www.samenacapital.com/overview.aspx

Samir is heavily involved in Samena Capital. He is on the board of directors and vice chairman of the Company and chairman of its executive committee. You will see it is a premier investment group focusing on investments in the sub-continent - Asia, Middle East and North Africa known as the Samena Region. This has a network of key players in corporate India and Asia which Samir thought would be of interest to you and your consulting business and he is happy to talk to you on this.

If you click on the link to the board of directors you will see some very interesting people they have associated with some great companies in this region such as Atul Punj who is chairman of the Punj Lloyd Group, India's second largest construction engineering company and Hari Shankar Singhania of the Singhania Group, one of India's leading pharmaceutical companies coming out of India. It also has a very interesting list of shareholders that are also listed on the website.

What would the time commitment be?

Post the induction period at the end of the month and the IPO board meetings, Samir thinks this would be realistically 12 days per annum.

What is the remuneration?

£60k per annum. Samir would like to deliver £300k if shares at 50% of the IPO value. This should be a very financeable deal and the Company would look to a friendly bank to provide the finance should you wish. We are still doing some work out how these could be given in a tax efficient manner. I will revert with more of the details mechanics when I have had further discussions with JP Morgan. The proposal may involve some of the shares only actually being issued to you a little further down the line so as to defer the tax might be payable.

Sorry this is all bit long. But what do you think?

P

Difficult to judge without seeing financial info - income statement, balance sheet, cash flow on toaz. I presume you've taken a look at this?

I think joining lazar is a mistake for the record.

messages.subject: SJ Plan Studies - Main Residence
messages.body:
Jeffrey,

Attached are three plan variations that address what we discussed last week.

Option A:
* This plan is similar to what we discussed, and your fixed sketch.
* We shifted the support building to be centered with the new living room.
* We opened up the walkway leading from the main residence to the new spaces.
* We are concerned about the overall size of the new living room with the added enclosed gallery space; it’s about 30’ x 40’.
* This plan may also require us to shift a portion of the roadway, but I do not think we have room at that area. I think the drop off on the north side of the road is pretty steep.

Option B:
* This combines the support spaces and living room into one building, and realigns them similar to what we discussed.
* This building also feels very large; it’s about 70’ x 30’.
* We also kept the small building north of the office, but it could be omitted, and the courtyard expanded.

Option C:
* This scheme seems to be the most efficient for overall building massing.
* We would expand the existing office, and create bathrooms, crafts, support, etc.
* The living room would stand on its own, 30’ x 50’.
* We may create a larger veranda on the west side of the living room.
* We do need to address the much larger deck on the east. This is the roof over the pool area. We do not think it should all be deck, perhaps a small part sheltered deck with “lookout” area (like the opposite side of the garden), and the rest landscape or roof over the pool below.

Please let me know your thoughts. We are working on the lower level plan diagrams for the pool and balcony.

Thanks,
Warwick

messages.body:
Jeffrey and Ghislaine: Notes on New York's Oldest Alliance - http://www.vanityfair.com/online/daily/2011/03/notes-on-new-yorks-oldest-couple-jeffrey-epstein-and-ghislaine-maxwell.html

By Vicky Ward | March 8, 2011, 2:30 PM

I've got a piece for Vanity Fair on Indonesia. Or New Orleans. Or both. Go there. I just have been. You will love it. I will talk you into it. We can do anything together. So spoke not Bill or Melinda Gates, but Ghislaine Maxwell, the 48-year-old daughter of the late British press baron Robert Maxwell. She is also, as it happens, the closest procurer of billionaire Jeffrey Epstein.

Jeffrey, 57, is the financier who spent a year in jail on charges of soliciting prostitutes and now there is talk of another investigation because various women, now in their twenties and thirties, have come forward with allegations that he molested them when they were under age. The allegations first surfaced in British newspapers, which were zeroed in on Epstein's alleged behavior on his private island in the Caribbean, Little St. James. I wrote a piece for Vanity Fair in 2003 called 'The Talent Spotter.' It was largely a business piece that focused on his mysterious exit from Bear Stearns in 1981. His close relationships with Jimmy Cayne, Les Wexner, the chairman of Limited Brands, and above all, the man who claimed to be his mentor, Steven Jude Hoffenberg, who is currently serving a 20-year jail sentence for bilking investors in Towers Financial out of $450 million.

The piece alluded to Epstein's great friendship with Maxwell, and how she introduced him to young women with whom he had sexual relationships. But, in the end, the story didn't quite hit on the issue that remains a mystery now: Jeffrey made his money, and how Ghislaine made hers.

This is not to say I didn't hear stories about the girls. I did. But, not knowing quite who to believe, I concentrated on the intriguing financial mystery instead. But now the women have come back. Not the same ones, different ones. And their stories are bone-chilling. Journalists from England have phoned and, in one case, flown to ask me about Epstein and Maxwell. Who is he? And the British, especially, want to know. Who is she? At this point, I am so bored of repeating myself to others it was, after all, my 2003 Vanity Fair story that brought him into the limelight that I have decided to write about them myself.

Bizarrely, perhaps, I have gotten to know Jeffrey and Ghislaine far better after my piece than before it. I kept running into both of them, separately, and, parties. Jeffrey is a social animal so he usually has a couple of young women with him who stand two feet behind him, as if serving a monarch. Do they speak? I remember asking him once, nodding at his lookalike blondes. He laughed. Not like you, Vicky, was his riposte.

I remembered that when we once discussed math in particular, an isosceles triangle and I revealed I hadn't studied math since I was 14 (such is, or was, the way of the British educational system), I received a package at home via messenger. It was a book: Math for idiots.

So he is not without humor, even though he doesn't drink or smoke, and hates restaurants.

Jeffrey knows a good deal about most subjects, newspaper publisher Mort Zuckerman told me last week. He was certainly knowing it to the converted. The truth is, Epstein does know a lot about a lot of things. Just a few moments in his company and you know this to be true.

When I saw pictures of Prince Andrew walking in Central Park with Jeffrey, my immediate thought was that Andy is Jeffrey's call sign. He is probably asking for help with his role as British trade envoy, or whatever his strange title is. Because if one thing is for sure: When it comes to international business, Jeffrey knows what he is talking about for more than Andy does. Which is why Leon Black, Mort Zuckerman and a few other financiers hang out with him.

And Ghislaine?

Full disclosure: I like her. Most people in New York do. It is almost impossible not to.

She is always the most interesting, the most vivacious, the most unusual person in any room. I've spent hours talking to her about the third world at a bar until 2am. She is passionate as she is knowledgeable. She is curious. She has spent weeks at the bottom of the ocean, literally going deeper than anyone else. She has sent me a DVD of the fish there. Her rolodex would blow away almost anyone else I can think of, probably even Rupert Murdoch's. She is very well read and can talk about most things for hours. She is passionate about Bill Clinton with whom she is close friends.

Yet, touchingly, when she shed tears at the 40th birthday party of her best friend, Ariadne Calvo-Platero, (known formerly as she was married to the 'Tennis Goddess') Ghislaine spoke a little with nerves. When it comes down to things she really cares about and Ariadne is one of them Ghislaine shows her vulnerability.

And that vulnerability is key to understanding her friendship with Jeffrey.

She said her, I remember a close friend of mine telling me. When her father died, she was a wreck, inconsolable. And then Jeffrey took in. She is never forgotten that. When her father died, she was a wreck, inconsolable. And then Jeffrey took in.

In many ways, the socially awkward Epstein with his big house, plane, island and ranch was the perfect replacement for her father, the late Robert Maxwell, newspaper tycoon and criminal. Sure, Jeffrey had his sexual peccadillos, but then Ghislaine's father was not without his oddities. After all, it was he who died leaving a massive black hole he fraudulently created. To Ghislaine, Jeffrey's habits may not have seemed that strange.

In fact, she probably figured, rather like I have, after years of writing about the very rich, that most successful people in the end either have some weird habit (the late Bruce Wasserstein had the weight issues, the girls issues, and moved countries to avoid paying tax), or they break the law (Sam Waksal, Martha Stewart). You don't tend to get to the top by playing by the rules. Epstein, for all his weirdness, has had a normal life and a normal life. He had a second wife for many years whose existence has been open about.

So what to make of the current fuss over Ghislaine? I haven't spoken to her or to Jeffrey, but I suspect that her loyalty to friends like Bill Clinton will keep her in good stead. In the end, she'll be out about as always. Look at Waksal and Stewart. No one sees them and thinks: criminal. Au contraire, this city, money makes up for all sorts of blemishes.

Thanks.

Sent from my BlackBerry wireless device

messages.subject: Three Day ON CAMERA Acting in FILMBIntensive
messages.body: LOS ANGELES with B JEAN-LOUIS RODRIGUE and KRISTOF KONRAD B B B NOV 11, 12, 13, 2011; 10:00 a.m. - 6:00 pm. B B Tuition: $450 B B B An actor's vision is lived emotionally and physically. B That kind of performance requires concentration, focus, and a mastery of physical, psychological, and emotional craft into performance. B Internationally acclaimed teachers Jean-Louis Rodrigue and Kristof Konrad invite you to join them for an intensive workshop to explore the skills and tools that are required for the extraordinary creation of characters and performances. B B Wheel of Knowledge; 1575 Westwood Blvd. B Los Angeles , CA 90024 B B Register call Kristof B B B COURSE CONTENT: B *Stage versus Film B *Acting B *Being in your Body, Ease and Availability B *Listening versus Performing B *Trusting That

The Alexander technique is invaluable to actors of all ages. It helps us find new depth in exploring the physical and emotional life of a character. And it has helped me correct physical issues which affect my daily life. Jean-Louis and Kristof immediately create an atmosphere of trust and safety. Their technique which allows all of us in the class to open up to the learning experience. I continue to work privately with them because I believe so strongly in their work. It has a positive effect on my well-being.

Jean-Louis Rodriguez is a popular movement coach in Los Angeles whose specialty is helping actors bring gracefulness and fluidity to their performances. A combination of acting coach, BAlexanderTechniqueTeacher and dance instructor, Jean-Louis brings techniques that have much in common with dance training. His teachings emphasize an awareness of the body and the physicality of performance. By helping actors to become more aware of their work as important as the intellectual, they become far more convincing and seamless.

The absolute best Alexander classes are given daily by my four-month old son. Kristof and Jean-Louis are a close second. They are not only expert in the theory and practice of the Alexander Technique, but they have a wonderful way of communicating their work with a vibrant, contagious love. Their endeavor to help performers choose a new physical life that allows them to be more fully present—in essence, to be more fully themselves—has implications not only for life on the stage, but for life in general. Kristof and Jean-Louis create a beautiful work environment: safe, rigorous, personal—and sprinkled with a healthy dose of humor. I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to work with them. And they don’t spit up nearly as much as my son!

Jean-Louis is a gifted teacher. Some teachers are able to adjust and produce results in students immediately. However, often their work does not have a lasting value. B Jean-Louis is not in that category. His understanding of the Alexander Technique and his ability to communicate it in such a way that he is able to leave a lasting impression on most of the actors he encounters. It is a pleasure to be able to testify to his skill, ability, and integrity.

Hi JEE... Two things: First, do any of the following weekends work for a visit to you? Sept 12-13 Sept 9-20 Oct 10-11 Oct 17-18 Second, here's a blurb on what I would like to do. (I've gotten a rise out of somebody at Columbia business school about this, but haven't followed it up -- meanwhile, I'm seeing one of the deans at the NYU business school in two weeks.) Translational Cognitive Studies Research in translational cognitive studies rests on three central premises: 1. Translational research: Theory guides applications to real-world situations. For example, theories of learning can be used to design new teaching methods. But, crucially, not only does theory lead to applications, but also the applications raise new research issues, which feed back to enrich theory. 2. Generative principles: Unlike most applied psychology, the goal here is not to solve specific problems (such as how best to design a control panel). Rather, the goal is to develop generative principles that can be applied across a domain; just as the rules of grammar can be used to produce an infinite number of sentences, these generative principles can produce a large range of applications within a domain. The "Cognitive Communication Principles" (summarized in my books on ways to use graphs and PowerPoint) are examples of this, rules of learning would be another example. 3. Cross-disciplinary: By its nature, such research draws on theory and findings from multiple disciplines, ranging from cognitive neuroscience to business and from education to economics and computer science. Indeed, even philosophy has a role to play, in helping to develop and home theory. At its outset, this research program has two foci, learning and visual communication. Both play key roles in virtually all human endeavors. Moreover, this research focuses on developing both products (typically software) and procedures (such as new ways to use existing technology in teaching).

The server room will be the next on the list when Scott integrates the server in. The ladders have been going floor to floor cleaning every inch of the house all closets included. I would like to have all shipping items picked up this coming week of 1/17/11 if possible. I have called Emmet and we will have a plumber out to check the water pressure in the steam boiler. We are working on a hot water heating problem that I discovered when the colder weather came in last week. The heating system upper heat Zones being supplied by AC-3 fan & the 5th floor fan units heating are losing water pressure effecting room temperatures on the 4th & 5th floors. After various trouble shooting tests I found the shell & tube Heat exchanger #2 has a tube leak and the heat hot water was leaking out water pressure through the steam condensate line. This was causing the Re heat hot water system pressure to drop and the re heat coils to get air bound and not working. We are operating Heat exchanger#1 with an extra steam bypass supply to make up the difference capacity all rooms are now making set points. I replaced Heat exchanger #1 tube bundle about 2 years ago. #2 tube bundle which is leaking is original to the house. The Source One project is also moving forward the full energy report and recommendations for system up grades will be complete by 1/25/11 I am also waiting on Pricing for up grades that AD Winston is working on for free cool & removal of the old Carrier Chiller and adding the additional 25 tons of cooling. subject: Life and a very long email

messages.subject: Life and a very long email
messages.body:
Dear Jeffrey,
Even though I'm older, in many ways you're wiser. So I'm asking your advice. I saw a new job/even yesterday and left my office in tears. He's insisting that I <REDACTED>.
Given my general state of anxiety about this issue, I was overwhelmed by his advice and approach. What do you think about:
Problem #1: I got an email from my management company in response to my request for upgrading the appliances, cabinets and electricity in my kitchen and they attached a 57-page document for me to fill out and informed me that there's a $1000 fee for them to approve the work plus a $2500 fee for security in case anything gets damaged in common areas. It's extortion. I worked so hard to get the cost of this project down and then an extra $3500 is thrown in for nothing. I felt very victimized. Problem #2: Being here this week on spring break, I realize I'd rather be working. I'm so bored and lonely. I'm thinking of going to a singles cruise. I know this all sounds crazy, but this week at home is making me realize that a 12-week summer vacation may not turn out so well. you need to back up your hot yoga benefits with real numbers . . . the doc's in new york see more hot yoga or iyengar devotees . . . than any other exercise regimen including weights

oh my . . . someone has been feeding you misinformation. first of all, we have a hypothalamus and the sweat that is released during hot yoga ensures that our internal organs and core temperature remains constant. second, it isn't endorphins that are released. It's more likely acetylcholine or nitric oxide. it's paradoxical because it is highly parasympathetic but still has elevated heart rate - probably as a result of the vagus nerve in check. it is very interesting that people who do yoga do not catch infectious disease, alzheimers or parkinsons. it's not the fake convese thing where you can say that adrenaline/parkinsons/sick people can't do yoga. it's biological. i've been doing hot yoga for 10 years and have never been sick. i think that because we are traditionally neurotransmitter-mediated, it's also super interesting that women who get botox and do hot yoga only have the effects of the botox for 2-4 weeks (1/3 the regular time). I've measured my temperature during yoga and tracked heart rate with an ekg. very interesting. too much to type! hang on more soon . . .

lots of science people . . . code breaking, signal processing, psychopharm, membrane computing . . . all fun. Hot yoga is not healthy, internal organ temp too high, of course you like it, endo-release up to kazoo. liver chem goes way off . . . Do you have a metric for success of the philanthropy. sounds great. salary billion dollars a day.

Well, I certainly have missed you. I know that you are a keen observer and probably took away some interesting lessons. I'm sorry that you had to go through all this crap - Are you still doing science? Some super cool stuff out there. I've also got some very crazy ideas of my own that we should talk about. Crazy even for me, but probably right. I think herpes causes a few types of heart disease and treating it prevents stroke and heart attack. Stuff like that! Since you've been out of the loop some interesting stuff has happened to me. I've been writing for the FT style section (under a fake name) and friendly with some of the fancy designer types. Good practice for me! Still working on Special Initiatives at the <REDACTED> and also reviewing the very crazy stuff that comes our way. I think you have a much better sense of the real vs. fake than I do. I manage several different portfolios of Special Projects whose grants/commitments total about $315M. It's crazy to think about the amount of money. Wow. In November I am doing my annual site visits in Africa (I try to do them all at once. Africa is a tough place to be) and during that time I will be in <REDACTED> for a week. I'm excited about that! Also still doing <REDACTED> and contemplating going back for more training (only because the non-invasive/high tech stuff is making me feel like a dinosaur!). I just don't want to leave my job and a little worried if I take any more time off they will fire me. Not sure what to do but ultimately, I think I have more longevity as a superbly trained <REDACTED> than I do working at <REDACTED>. <REDACTED> is doing fine - we just celebrated being together 3 years. Who would've thought? He's way up there at <REDACTED> these days and pretty much hates his job. I discovered hot yoga after all these years. Love it! Well, I think that's about it for the past few months that you have been away. I really have missed you a lot. Hope that you are starting to feel back to normal and if there is anything I can do for you please let me know?

messages.subject: Robin Hood/Cannes
messages.body:
On Sat, May 8, 2010 at 8:39 AM, Peggy Siegal <peggy@peggysiegel.com> wrote:

#1 I would love to go to Robin Hood and can sit at any table. Hopefully I might know some of the people that are there.

#2 IPP (independent filmmakers project) Spring Gala at Diane von Furstenberg's honoring her daughter Tatiana...was a blast. I had a blast. Film clips of her life and a floor of black and white photos of her that a disaster for 180 downstaris in the high white photo gallery with long tables covered with hot charcuterie cloths and piles of light italian food down the center. It was fabulous. Very large photos of movie and rock stars lined the walls. Oliver Stone, Warren Beatty, and sons of young terrific hip filmmakers (and models, artists, photographers, fashion designers) that we cultivate came. All the kids all had and then walked a block to the Boom Boom Room till 2:00am. Got tons of press. Joaquin gave us $10,000 worth of wine from his own Napa Valley vineyard. Kids drinking $100 bottles of wine. The food was catered by a fabulous Italian restaurant in the West Village. The whole room was a disaster. The film clip group, Seygler is a complete creep. He has no personality. Sort of like a zombie on a drig. We had smart directors sitting next to him and his idiot gorgeous wife and could not get any conversation out of him except 'I have a yacht I am taking to St. Tropez.'

I walked him around and he was so weird that even I ran away from him. There is an obvious personal discontent and I don't think I can just take him money and deliver a better life because he has no feel for social behavior. Diane was thrilled to have him there and he was a total disaster. The New York Times photographer Bill Cunningham and the next Sunday her photo spread was a social/cultural disaster and people began to believe she is 'special'. Her gala was filled with hack rich people like Bob Iger a complete jerk. The whole scene is a bad joke with the higher echelon of cultivation of the arts. He has always had a very low regard for the manufactured 'art scene'.

#3 Cannes. The Carlton. I want to four top designers and get the most gorgeous gowns. I have put together a schedule of the best films and parties. I am excited about writing my '3rd Cannes Diary. and already dreaming about the parties. I am going to have a dawn outside my window overlooking the dark snail sky. Just kidding. Just kidding. Just kidding I am going.

Trying to lay low this weekend to get rid of my cold. Sending my idiot brother, his idiot wife, my idiot mother and my recovering niece to 'Lend Me A Tenor' Sunday matinee and dreading meeting them at the Jean George restaurant in the new Mark Hotel.

Home most of the day. xoxo Peg
